# Glossary

Every term the book defines, in alphabetical order, with the chapter that teaches it. The definitions are short reminders; the chapter has the full explanation, the derivation and the examples. If a term in an explanation is unclear, look it up here before reading further.

## A

**ablation**: removing or adding the components of a method one at a time (or in a grid) under the same protocol to see which of them produce the result; when components interact, the grid is the report and shares of the gain are not defined. *([Experiments, Baselines and Claims](v02-learning/08-experiments.md))*

**absolute position embedding**: a table with one trained vector for each position, added to the token's embedding before the first layer, so that the same word at two places enters the network as two different vectors; it cannot name a position beyond its last row. *([Positional Information](v05-sequences/08-positions.md))*

**accuracy**: the share of a classifier's decisions that are right, $(\mathrm{TP} + \mathrm{TN})/N$; equivalently the average of the per-class success rates weighted by the class shares, so a rare class barely affects it. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**activation function**: the fixed one-input function $g$ a neuron applies to its weighted sum to produce its output, for example the identity, the sigmoid or the step. *([The Neuron and the Perceptron](v03-neural-networks/01-perceptron.md))*

**Adam**: an update that steps along a bias-corrected running average of the gradient divided by the root of a bias-corrected running average of its square, keeping two state arrays per parameter. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**AdamW**: Adam with decoupled weight decay: $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \eta\lambda\theta - \eta\hat{\mathbf{m}}/(\sqrt{\hat{\mathbf{v}}} + \epsilon_{\mathrm{den}})$. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**adaptive computation**: letting the amount of computation depend on the input, here through a learned probability, read from each pass's state, of stopping at that pass, which weights the loss and selects how many passes a token receives. *([Looped and Recurrent-Depth Transformers](v06-language-models/07-recurrent-depth.md))*

**adaptive layer normalization**: a normalization layer whose scale and shift (and, around a sublayer, whose gate) are computed from a conditioning vector such as the timestep embedding instead of being learned constants; a zero gate makes the block the identity. *([Denoiser Architectures: U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers](v08-image-generation/08-denoiser-architectures.md))*

**additive attention**: attention whose score for a decoder state and an encoder state is computed by a small network that adds a projection of each before a tanh and takes a weighted sum of the result, so that the decoder can build a different weighted average of the encoder states at every step. *([Encoder-Decoder Models and the Birth of Attention](v05-sequences/06-seq2seq.md))*

**adversarial loss**: the pair of losses in which a discriminator minimizes a classification loss on real and fake samples while the generator minimizes a loss on the discriminator's score of its samples, each holding the other fixed. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**affine quantization**: the map from a real number to an $n_b$-bit integer code and back, $q = \mathrm{clamp}(\mathrm{round}(w/\Delta) + q_0, 0, 2^{n_b} - 1)$ and $w' = \Delta(q - q_0)$, a multiplication and an offset applied to a group of weights. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**aggregate posterior**: the distribution of codes obtained when a reading is chosen at random from the data and encoded, the average of the per-reading posteriors over the data; the KL term of the bound splits into a part that measures how much the code tells about the reading and a part that measures how far this average lies from the prior. *([Variational Autoencoders](v08-image-generation/02-vae.md))*

**ahead-of-time compilation**: compiling kernels for a list of known device architectures before the program ships and loading the results at run time with a key that identifies their inputs, so that a machine without a compiler can run them, at the price of storage and of devices outside the list. *([One Program, Many Devices](v04-computation/09-backends.md))*

**algorithm**: a finite list of definite steps that turns any input of a stated kind into an output of a stated kind, whose correctness can be argued with an invariant that holds before and after every pass of its loops. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**aliasing**: the confusion, after sampling, of a tone above half the sampling rate with a slower one, because the two have the same samples. *([Sound and Sampling](v09-audio/01-sound.md))*

**Amdahl's law**: the speedup of a whole from making a part that takes the share $p$ of the time $g$ times as fast, $1/((1 - p) + p/g)$, bounded by the ceiling $1/(1 - p)$ however fast the part becomes. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**amortized inference**: using one encoder network, with shared weights, to produce the approximate posterior of every reading in a single forward pass, so that the cost of finding a good guess is paid once in training and not again for each new reading. *([Variational Autoencoders](v08-image-generation/02-vae.md))*

**ancestral sampling**: drawing the variables of a model one at a time, parents before children, each from its distribution given the values already drawn, so that the joint draw follows the product of the conditionals. *([What It Means to Generate](v08-image-generation/01-generative-modeling.md))*

**anchor-free detection**: a detector whose every cell, with its anchor point at the cell centre, predicts its box as the distances from that point to the four sides, with no template boxes and no objectness score. *([Object Detection](v07-vision/04-detection.md))*

**angular margin loss**: a classification loss on cosines in which the embedding and the class centres are normalized, the logits are scaled by a constant, and a fixed margin is added to the angle between the sample and its own centre, so that the sample is asked to be closer to its centre by that angle than the plain classifier requires. *([Faces: Detection, Identity and Parsing](v07-vision/11-faces.md))*

**architecture hypothesis testing**: deciding whether a new architectural idea is worth anything by a hypothesis and a margin stated before the run, a baseline that differs from the candidate in exactly one thing, equal tuning and paired seeds, an ablation of the part the idea is named for, and an effect size with its interval judged against the margin. *([A Research Architecture: The Spectral Language Model](v06-language-models/09-spectral-lm.md))*

**arithmetic intensity**: the number of floating-point operations a computation performs per byte it must move between main memory and the arithmetic, a property of the algorithm and the sizes and formats and not of the machine. *([Memory Bandwidth, Compute and the Roofline](v04-computation/03-roofline.md))*

**artificial neuron**: a function of an input vector that forms a weighted sum of its entries plus a bias and passes the total through an activation function, $y = g(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{x} + b)$; the weights and the bias are what is learned. *([The Neuron and the Perceptron](v03-neural-networks/01-perceptron.md))*

**asymptotic complexity**: the growth rate of an algorithm's cost as the size of its input grows, stated with $O$, $\Omega$ and $\Theta$ so that constants and lower-order terms are dropped and only the shape (such as $n$, $n \log n$ or $n^2$) remains. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**attention backward**: the gradient of attention, obtained by undoing in order the weighted average, the softmax rule on each row, the score product with its scale and the three projections, with the input collecting three contributions and no step of its own for the mask. *([Self-Attention](v05-sequences/07-self-attention.md))*

**attention injection**: adding the result of a second attention, over extra tokens with their own keys and values, to the context of an attention site (or to the residual stream where no site exists) with a strength, so that at strength zero the site's output is exactly what it was. *([Control, Identity and Adapters](v08-image-generation/11-control-and-identity.md))*

**attention sink**: a key, usually at one of the first positions of the text, that most queries score high whatever their content and whose value is near zero, so that the softmax has somewhere to put its mass; a window that keeps the sink beside its recent keys keeps this behaviour. *([Attention Variants: Sharing and Compressing Keys](v06-language-models/03-attention-variants.md))*

**attentive statistics pooling**: a pooling over time that learns a weight for each frame of each channel, by a softmax over a score from a small network, and returns the weighted mean and weighted standard deviation of every channel. *([Who Is Speaking](v09-audio/05-speaker-embeddings.md))*

**audio resampling**: computing the samples of a recording at a new rate, by removing the frequencies the new rate cannot carry and evaluating the band-limited signal at the new sample times as a weighted sum of the old samples. *([Sound and Sampling](v09-audio/01-sound.md))*

**audio token**: one integer of a codec's output, an index into one stage's table for one column, which a language model treats as a symbol. *([Neural Audio Codecs](v09-audio/03-audio-codecs.md))*

**autoencoder**: a network trained to output its own input after passing it through a bottleneck layer much narrower than the input, so that it must learn a short code from which the input can be rebuilt. *([First Complete Models](v03-neural-networks/13-first-models.md))*

**autoregressive factorization**: writing the probability of a sequence as the product, over its positions, of the probability of each token given all the tokens before it, an identity that holds for every distribution over sequences. *([Language Modeling](v05-sequences/04-language-modeling.md))*

## B

**backend abstraction**: the narrow set of operations (capabilities, compile, create a buffer, upload, dispatch, read back, release) that every device-specific backend provides with the same meaning, so that the code that builds a model never names the device that runs it. *([One Program, Many Devices](v04-computation/09-backends.md))*

**backpropagation through time**: the backward pass on a recurrent network unrolled over the steps of a sequence, in which the gradient of the state is passed back one step at a time and the gradients of the shared weights are summed over the steps. *([Recurrent Networks](v05-sequences/05-recurrent-networks.md))*

**backward pass**: visiting the nodes of the graph in reverse order, multiplying the gradient that arrives from the next quantity by the local derivative and adding contributions where a value is used more than once. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**backward pass of a broadcast**: the rule that sums the incoming gradient over every axis the forward pass stretched, so a copy in the forward becomes a sum in the backward. *([The Backward Pass of Every Layer](v03-neural-networks/05-layer-gradients.md))*

**backward pass of a linear layer**: the three rules $d\mathbf{X} = d\mathbf{Y}\mathbf{W}$, $d\mathbf{W} = d\mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{X}$ and $d\mathbf{b} = \sum_b d\mathbf{Y}$ for $\mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{X}\mathbf{W}^\top + \mathbf{b}$, each gradient having the shape of the array it belongs to. *([The Backward Pass of Every Layer](v03-neural-networks/05-layer-gradients.md))*

**backward pass of a matrix multiply**: for $\mathbf{C} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{B}$, the gradients $d\mathbf{A} = d\mathbf{C}\mathbf{B}^\top$ and $d\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{A}^\top d\mathbf{C}$, two matrix products of the forward's size; for a batch, the same per item, summed over the batch for an operand shared by all items. *([The Backward Pass of Every Layer](v03-neural-networks/05-layer-gradients.md))*

**backward pass of a reduction**: the rule that sends the gradient of a sum, mean or maximum back to the entries that were collapsed: copied for a sum, divided by the count for a mean, routed to the argmax for a maximum. *([The Backward Pass of Every Layer](v03-neural-networks/05-layer-gradients.md))*

**backward pass of an elementwise function**: multiplying the incoming gradient entry by entry with the derivative of the function at the input, $dx = dy\,f'(x)$, which needs the input, the output or a mask saved from the forward. *([The Backward Pass of Every Layer](v03-neural-networks/05-layer-gradients.md))*

**bandwidth-bound**: limited by the bytes it moves: the arithmetic intensity is below the machine's ridge point, so the attainable rate is intensity times bandwidth and only moving fewer bytes makes it faster. *([Memory Bandwidth, Compute and the Roofline](v04-computation/03-roofline.md))*

**baseline**: a method run under the same protocol as the new one, trivial (no features), simple (an earlier chapter's method fitted properly) or the previous best, whose result the new one must beat to count as progress. *([Experiments, Baselines and Claims](v02-learning/08-experiments.md))*

**batch dimension**: an extra, usually first, axis of a tensor that indexes independent examples processed together, so that each example is one contiguous block. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**batch-normalization**: normalizing each feature of a layer's output with the mean and variance taken over the examples of the batch, then applying a learned gain and shift; it keeps running averages of the statistics for use at prediction time. *([Normalization Layers](v03-neural-networks/10-normalization.md))*

**Bayes' rule**: the identity $P(A \mid B) = P(B \mid A)P(A)/P(B)$ that turns the probability of evidence given a cause into the probability of the cause given the evidence, using the prior probability of the cause. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**beam search**: keeping the $B$ partial texts of highest total log-probability at every step instead of one, to find a more probable whole text than greedy decoding does, at $B$ times the work. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**Bernoulli distribution**: the distribution of a single yes/no outcome coded as $1$ or $0$, equal to $1$ with probability $p$; its mean is $p$ and its variance is $p(1-p)$. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**bf16 format**: the 16-bit floating-point layout of 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (the exponent field of fp32) and 7 fraction bits: fp32's range with 2.4 digits, obtained from an fp32 by dropping the low 16 bits (with rounding). *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**bias correction**: dividing an exponential average that started at zero by $1 - \beta^t$, which removes the start-up bias toward zero so that the early averages and the first steps have the right size. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**bias-variance tradeoff**: the exact split of the expected squared error into noise, squared bias (what the model family cannot express) and variance (how much the fit moves between training sets), and the fact that making a model more flexible lowers the first of the last two and raises the second. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**bidirectional encoder**: a stack of transformer blocks whose attention uses the full mask, so that the vector at every position is computed from every token of the text, to the left and to the right, in every layer; it gives a vector per token in one pass and cannot generate left to right. *([Bidirectional Encoders and Embedding Models](v05-sequences/14-encoders.md))*

**binary cross-entropy**: the loss $-[y\log\hat{p} + (1 - y)\log(1 - \hat{p})]$ for a yes-or-no label $y$ and predicted probability $\hat{p}$, the cross-entropy of a Bernoulli outcome; in terms of the logit $z$ it is $\mathrm{softplus}(z) - y z$. *([Classification and Logistic Regression](v02-learning/03-logistic-regression.md))*

**binary representation**: writing a non-negative whole number as bits, each with a place value that is a power of 2, so that $n$ bits give the $2^n$ numbers $0 \dots 2^n - 1$ and arithmetic on them wraps modulo $2^n$. *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**BiSeNet**: a segmentation network with two paths, a shallow spatial path that keeps one eighth of the resolution to place boundaries and a fast-shrinking context path with a global pool that supplies the meaning, joined by a learned fusion and followed by a head that predicts per-pixel class scores. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**blind restoration**: restoration in which the degradation that produced the input is not given and varies from picture to picture, so that the restorer must work without being told what was done, in practice by being trained on a wide family of degradations. *([Restoration and Super-Resolution](v08-image-generation/12-restoration.md))*

**bootstrap**: a method that estimates the sampling distribution of a statistic by repeatedly drawing a sample of the same size with replacement from the sample itself and recomputing the statistic, giving a standard error or interval without a formula. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**bounding box**: the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that holds an object, written as corners $(x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2)$, as a centre and size $(c_x, c_y, w, h)$, or in either form divided by the image size; a box covers the pixels $x_1 \le x < x_2$, $y_1 \le y < y_2$. *([Object Detection](v07-vision/04-detection.md))*

**box regression loss**: a loss on the difference between a predicted box and the true one; the IoU family (1 minus the IoU, GIoU, DIoU or CIoU) measures it by overlap, and adds terms so that boxes that do not overlap still receive a gradient. *([Object Detection](v07-vision/04-detection.md))*

**broadcasting**: the rule that aligns two shapes from the right and treats an axis of size 1 as stretched to match the other, by giving it stride 0, so that arrays of different shapes combine without copying. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**buffer alignment**: the rule that a value starts at an address that is a multiple of its alignment, which fixes where the fields of a parameter block and the slices of a buffer may begin and leaves padding between them. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**bundle adjustment**: the joint nonlinear least-squares refinement of every camera pose, every 3D point and optionally the calibration against the observed pixels, solved by Levenberg-Marquardt with the points eliminated by the Schur complement, and fixing the gauge. *([Structure from Motion and Multi-View Stereo](v10-video-and-3d/04-structure-from-motion.md))*

**byte-level BPE**: byte-pair encoding whose starting symbols are the 256 byte values of a text's UTF-8, so no piece of any input is unknown; GPT-2-style files spell each byte as a printable stand-in character. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**byte-pair encoding**: a way to learn a vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent pair of adjacent symbols, and to encode text by replaying those merges in the order they were learned. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

## C

**cache equivalence**: the property that running a text as a prefill followed by cached decode steps gives the same logits as one forward pass over the whole text, exactly when the arithmetic is the same and to a stated tolerance when only the order of the sums differs. *([The KV Cache](v05-sequences/12-kv-cache.md))*

**cache hierarchy**: the stack of memories between a core's registers and main memory, each level larger and slower than the one above it and holding copies of the lines most recently used from the level below. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**cache line**: the aligned block of memory, 64 bytes on most chips, that is fetched and kept in a cache as a unit when any of its bytes is needed. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**calibration**: the property that a model's probabilities match frequencies, so that among the examples given probability $p$ about a share $p$ are positive; measured with a reliability diagram and the expected calibration error. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**calibration set**: the sample of inputs that is run through the float graph to record the range of every tensor; it must be representative of the deployment, because a range that is too narrow clamps real values and one that is too wide wastes codes. *([Neural Processing Units and Graph Compilers](v04-computation/13-npu.md))*

**camera extrinsics**: the rotation and translation that carry a world point into the camera's own frame, six numbers that say where the camera stood and which way it faced for one photograph. *([Cameras and Projective Geometry](v10-video-and-3d/03-camera-geometry.md))*

**camera intrinsics**: the numbers that belong to the camera itself and hold for every photograph it takes: the focal lengths in pixels along the two image axes and the principal point, collected in the matrix $\mathbf{K}$, together with the lens coefficients that bend the ray. *([Cameras and Projective Geometry](v10-video-and-3d/03-camera-geometry.md))*

**capability declaration**: the statement of what a device can execute correctly, queried from the device and absent when unknown, matched against what each candidate needs, so that a candidate that cannot run is removed before any cost is considered. *([Choosing the Fastest Correct Kernel](v04-computation/10-kernel-selection.md))*

**catastrophic cancellation**: the loss of leading digits when two nearly equal numbers that carry rounding errors are subtracted; the subtraction is exact but promotes the earlier errors to the leading digits of a much smaller result, losing about $\log_{10}$ of the ratio of the operands to the result. *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

**categorical distribution**: a table of $K$ non-negative probabilities summing to $1$, one per outcome of a choice among $K$ possibilities such as the next word; the case $K = 2$ is the Bernoulli distribution. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**causal 3D convolution**: a convolution over height, width and time whose output at one time uses only that time and earlier ones, the missing earlier frames at the start of a clip being copies of the first. *([Video as Data](v10-video-and-3d/01-video.md))*

**causal language model**: a model whose output at each position depends only on the tokens up to that position and gives the distribution of the next one, so that its probabilities multiply into a valid probability of a sequence; in the data it means that the targets are the inputs shifted by one place. *([Language Modeling](v05-sequences/04-language-modeling.md))*

**causal mask**: the matrix of zeros and minus infinities added to the scores before the softmax so that position $i$ gives no weight to positions after it, which makes the output at each position a function of its prefix alone and lets all positions of a sequence be trained in one pass. *([Self-Attention](v05-sequences/07-self-attention.md))*

**central difference**: the finite difference $(f(x+h) - f(x-h))/(2h)$, whose error is proportional to $h^2$ because the first error term cancels by symmetry. *([Proving Gradients Correct](v03-neural-networks/06-gradient-checking.md))*

**central limit theorem**: the statement that the average of many independent draws with finite variance, shifted by the mean and divided by $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$, has a distribution that approaches the standard Gaussian whatever the distribution of the draws. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**chain rule**: the derivative of a composition is the derivative of the outer function, evaluated at the inner value, times the derivative of the inner function: $(f\circ g)'(x) = f'(g(x))\,g'(x)$. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**character encoding**: an agreement that maps characters to numbers and numbers to bytes, so that a sequence of bytes can be read back as the text it was written from; ASCII, the code pages and UTF-8 are examples. *([Text as Data](v05-sequences/01-text.md))*

**chat template**: the fixed rule that writes a list of role-tagged messages as one string framed by special tokens, so that it encodes to the one id sequence a model was trained on. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**checkpoint format**: the layout of a trained model in a file: which names, shapes and number formats it holds, and where the bytes of each tensor are, so that a reader that has never seen the file can find and decode them. *([Importing Pretrained Models and Proving Parity](v06-language-models/02-importing-models.md))*

**chunked recurrence**: computing a recurrence over groups of $C$ tokens, with a triangular solve and matrix products inside a group and the state passed only between groups, which gives the same outputs with fewer sequential steps and less state traffic. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**classification**: predicting which of a fixed set of categories an example belongs to, from its features, learned from labelled examples; with two categories, labelled $0$ and $1$, it is binary classification. *([Classification and Logistic Regression](v02-learning/03-logistic-regression.md))*

**classifier-free guidance**: sampling with the prediction $u_{\mathrm{un}} + g(u_c - u_{\mathrm{un}})$, the prediction made with the prompt pushed away from the prediction made without it by a scale $g$; $g = 1$ is the plain conditional model, and a larger $g$ follows the prompt harder at the cost of variety and of a second network pass per step. *([Samplers and Guidance](v08-image-generation/07-samplers-and-guidance.md))*

**codebook**: a table of $K$ vectors of $d$ numbers each, the only values a quantized vector may take; a position of a tokenizer stores the index of a row. *([Discrete Latents and Vector Quantization](v08-image-generation/03-vector-quantization.md))*

**codebook prior**: a learned codebook of clean-picture parts used as the space of allowed restorations, so that every restored feature is one of the codes the decoder was trained on and the codes are chosen from the whole degraded picture. *([Restoration and Super-Resolution](v08-image-generation/12-restoration.md))*

**codec language model**: a causal language model whose vocabulary is the codes of a neural audio codec and whose context carries the text and the voice, so that it writes audio as a sequence of codes that the codec's decoder turns into a waveform. *([Speech Synthesis](v09-audio/06-speech-synthesis.md))*

**color space**: the rule that turns a triple of numbers into a colour, made of three primary colours, a white point and a transfer curve, so that the same triple is a different colour in a different space. *([Images as Data](v07-vision/01-images.md))*

**command recording**: appending many dispatches to one list and handing the list to the device as a single submission, so that the host pays the submission cost once instead of once per dispatch; a read-back or any other observation of the device ends the list. *([Kernel Fusion and Memory Traffic](v04-computation/08-fusion.md))*

**compensated summation**: a way of adding many numbers in which a second variable carries the rounding error of each addition into the next, so that the error of the total stays near $2u$ times the sum of absolute values however many terms there are (Kahan's algorithm). *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

**complex number**: a point of the plane written $a + bi$, added like a vector and multiplied by the rule $(ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i$, which turns by the angle of one factor and stretches by its length; $i = (0, 1)$ is a quarter turn and $i^2 = -1$. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**composition**: feeding the output of one function into another, $(g \circ f)(x) = g(f(x))$; it is associative but not commutative. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

**computational graph**: a record of a calculation as nodes (values) and edges showing which values were used to compute which. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**compute kernel**: the program that one invocation of a data-parallel computation runs, together with the declaration of the buffers and constants it is given, written once and launched over a grid of workgroups. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**compute-bound**: limited by arithmetic: the arithmetic intensity is at or above the machine's ridge point, so the attainable rate is the peak arithmetic rate and only fewer or cheaper operations, or a faster unit, make it faster. *([Memory Bandwidth, Compute and the Roofline](v04-computation/03-roofline.md))*

**condition number**: for a bowl-shaped function, the ratio of its largest to its smallest curvature; a large ratio means long, narrow contours and slow progress for a fixed step size. The floating-point chapter extends the idea to how strongly a computation amplifies small errors in its inputs. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**conditional probability**: the probability of an event within the part of the experiment where another event occurred, $P(A \mid B) = P(A \cap B)/P(B)$, defined when $P(B) > 0$. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**confidence interval**: a range computed from a sample, $\bar{x} \pm 1.96\,\mathrm{SE}$ at level $95\%$, built by a recipe that contains the true value in about that share of repeated experiments. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**config default**: the value a reader substitutes for a field a configuration omits, which is a guess about the publisher: loud when the field fixes a shape and silent when it only changes a value. *([Importing Pretrained Models and Proving Parity](v06-language-models/02-importing-models.md))*

**conformer**: an encoder block in which attention and a convolution module sit between two half-step feed-forwards, so that it relates both distant rows and close ones. *([Speech Recognition](v09-audio/04-speech-recognition.md))*

**connectionist temporal classification**: a loss and a decoding rule for a model that writes a distribution over a vocabulary and a blank at every row, scoring a transcript by the total probability of all the paths that collapse to it. *([Speech Recognition](v09-audio/04-speech-recognition.md))*

**context extension**: making a model trained on texts of one length usable at a longer one, by choosing a scaling table for the new length and, usually, continuing to train it on texts of that length. *([Long Context](v06-language-models/08-long-context.md))*

**context vector**: the vector that carries what an encoder has read to the decoder; in the first design a single vector, the encoder's last state, and in attention a vector of its own at every output step, a weighted average of the encoder states. *([Encoder-Decoder Models and the Birth of Attention](v05-sequences/06-seq2seq.md))*

**contrastive loss**: a loss that trains vectors by comparison: for each anchor it is the softmax cross-entropy, at a temperature, over the cosines of the anchor to its partner and to the partners of the other pairs of the batch (the in-batch negatives), which raises the cosine of the pair and lowers the others. *([Bidirectional Encoders and Embedding Models](v05-sequences/14-encoders.md))*

**contrastive pretraining**: training two networks, here one for pictures and one for captions, so that the vectors they write into a shared space are close for the two members of a pair and far for the members of different pairs, with the other pairs of the batch as the negatives. *([Contrastive Vision-Language Learning](v07-vision/08-clip.md))*

**controlled experiment**: a comparison in which the two arms differ only in the thing the claim is about, with the data, recipe, seeds, compute, tuning effort and metric held the same, so that a difference can be attributed to that thing. *([Experiments, Baselines and Claims](v02-learning/08-experiments.md))*

**ControlNet**: a trainable copy of a frozen generator's down and middle blocks, fed a control signal (an image brought to the latent grid) and joined to the generator by zero convolutions whose outputs are added to its skip entries and middle activation, so that a pose, an edge map or a depth map steers generation while the generator's own weights stay as they are. *([Control, Identity and Adapters](v08-image-generation/11-control-and-identity.md))*

**convergence**: the approach of the iterates to the minimiser and of the loss to its minimum; for a quadratic loss it is geometric, with a speed set by the learning rate and the condition number. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**convexity**: the property that no chord joining two points of the curve lies below the curve, equivalent for twice-differentiable functions to a non-negative second derivative; every critical point of a convex function is a global minimum. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**ConvFFN**: a feed-forward network for feature maps: a depthwise $7 \times 7$ convolution with normalization, then two $1 \times 1$ convolutions that widen the channels by a factor (4) and narrow them again with a GELU between them. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**convolution backward**: the gradients of a convolution layer, the weight gradient as a sum over all positions of the output gradient times the input patch (a correlation of the input with $dy$) and the input gradient as the output gradient spread back through the kernel (a full correlation with the turned kernel, col2im of $d\mathbf{Y}^\top\mathbf{W}$). *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**convolution theorem**: the fact that the discrete Fourier transform of a circular convolution of two signals is the pointwise product of their transforms, so that convolution acts independently on each frequency and a long convolution can be computed with three fast transforms. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**convolutional network**: a network built from convolutions, nonlinearities and pooling (or strided convolutions) that shrinks a picture's maps while widening their channels until one output sees the whole picture and a linear layer reads it. *([Convolutional Networks and Residual Learning](v07-vision/03-cnns.md))*

**cooperative matrix**: a small matrix whose elements are held jointly by the invocations of one subgroup and operated on by subgroup-wide load, multiply-add and store operations; the programming interface to tensor cores, available only where the device reports the shapes and types it supports. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**cosine schedule**: a decay of the learning rate from its peak to a floor along half a period of the cosine, $\eta_{\min} + (\eta_{\max} - \eta_{\min})\tfrac12(1 + \cos\pi u)$, which starts and ends with zero slope. *([Learning-Rate Schedules and Gradient Clipping](v03-neural-networks/08-schedules-and-clipping.md))*

**cosine similarity**: the dot product of two vectors after dividing each by its norm, a number from $-1$ to $1$ that ignores positive scaling. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**covariance**: the expected product of the deviations of two variables from their means, $\mathbb{E}[XY] - \mathbb{E}[X]\mathbb{E}[Y]$, positive when they tend to move together; it is the cross term in the variance of a sum and the entry of the covariance matrix. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**CPU core**: one unit of a processor that fetches, decodes and executes instructions in a pipeline, with its own registers and first-level caches, sharing the rest of the memory system with the other cores of the chip. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**critical point**: a point where the derivative is zero, so the tangent is horizontal; it may be a minimum, a maximum or neither. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**cross-attention**: attention in which the questions come from one sequence, such as the decoder's states, and the things looked up come from another, such as the encoder's states; the general form of which additive attention is the first example. *([Encoder-Decoder Models and the Birth of Attention](v05-sequences/06-seq2seq.md))*

**cross-backend parity**: the property that every backend gives results for the same inputs that agree to a stated criterion, bit for bit where the kernel fixes every rounding and order, and otherwise within a tolerance derived from the error bound of the operation. *([One Program, Many Devices](v04-computation/09-backends.md))*

**cross-entropy**: the expected surprise under a belief $q$ of data drawn from $p$, $H(p, q) = -\sum_k p_k \log q_k$, the average code length paid for believing $q$; it is never below $H(p)$. *([Information, Entropy and Surprise](v01-mathematics/13-information-theory.md))*

**cross-validation**: estimating the error on new rows by dividing the data into $k$ folds, fitting to all but one fold and scoring on the one left out, in turn, and averaging the $k$ scores. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

## D

**data augmentation**: training on altered copies of the examples, with their labels kept, where the alteration encodes a known invariance of the task; an alteration that changes the true label adds wrong training data. *([Regularization in Neural Networks](v03-neural-networks/11-regularization.md))*

**data leakage**: any route by which information about the rows used for scoring reaches the fitting (duplicates, statistics computed from all the rows, the future, the same subject on both sides), which makes the score too good to be true. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**data-parallel loop**: a loop in which no iteration reads anything another iteration writes, so its iterations can be run in any order or at the same time with the same result; the `parallel for` of the book's pseudocode. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**dataset**: a collection of $N$ examples, each a vector of features paired with a label, written as the pairs $(\mathbf{x}_n, y_n)$. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**dead code**: a code of a codebook that is never the nearest to any encoder row, so that it receives no gradient, is never chosen again and costs bits in the format while buying nothing; it is revived by moving it onto an encoder row. *([Discrete Latents and Vector Quantization](v08-image-generation/03-vector-quantization.md))*

**dead-units**: ReLU units whose pre-activation is not positive on any input, so that their output and slope are zero, their incoming gradient is exactly zero and no gradient step can revive them. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**decision boundary**: the set of inputs where the model switches its decision, for a linear logit the line, plane or flat sheet $\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{x} = 0$ (at threshold $1/2$), which separates the two predicted classes. *([Classification and Logistic Regression](v02-learning/03-logistic-regression.md))*

**decision tree**: a model that asks a sequence of yes-or-no questions, each a threshold on one feature chosen to make the answers as informative about the class as possible, and predicts the class held at the leaf reached. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**decode phase**: generating one token at a time, each step running one row through the model, appending one key and one value per layer to the cache and attending to everything in it; limited by the bytes of the weights and the cache. *([The KV Cache](v05-sequences/12-kv-cache.md))*

**decoupled weight decay**: shrinking every weight by the factor $1 - \eta\lambda$ directly, outside the gradient and the adaptive scaling, so that the decay means the same for every parameter. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**delta rule**: updating a key-value memory by the outer product of the key and the prediction error, $\mathbf{S} \leftarrow \mathbf{S} + \beta\,\mathbf{k}(\mathbf{v} - \mathbf{S}^\top\mathbf{k})^\top$, one gradient step of a regression of the value on the key, so that a write replaces what the key returned. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**denoising objective**: the training loss of a diffusion model: the mean squared error between the network's output for a noisy input and the target that the noising supplied, averaged over the data, the step and the noise. *([Diffusion Models](v08-image-generation/05-diffusion.md))*

**density estimation**: choosing from a family of candidate distributions the one that best explains observed data, usually by maximizing the likelihood and judging it by the likelihood of data that were held out. *([What It Means to Generate](v08-image-generation/01-generative-modeling.md))*

**depth-vs-width**: the tradeoff between a network of many layers and one of few wide layers; for the sawtooth, $d$ layers of width $2$ make $2^d$ linear pieces, while one layer with $u$ units makes at most $u + 1$. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**depthwise convolution**: a convolution that gives every channel its own single kernel and sums nothing across channels (a grouped convolution with as many groups as channels); followed by a pointwise convolution it replaces a dense layer with a fraction $1/C_{\mathrm{out}} + 1/k^2$ of its parameters. *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**derivative**: the limit of the difference quotient $\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$ as $h \to 0$; the slope of the tangent to the curve of $f$ at $x$, and the rate at which $f$ changes when $x$ changes. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**determinant**: the signed factor by which a square matrix scales area or volume ($ad - bc$ for a $2 \times 2$); zero exactly when the matrix crushes space and has no inverse. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**deterministic sampler**: a sampler whose output is a function of its starting noise alone, with no random draw after the first, so that the same noise always gives the same image; the step that re-noises the denoiser's guess to the next level with the noise the old level implies, and Euler's method on the velocity field, are such samplers. *([Samplers and Guidance](v08-image-generation/07-samplers-and-guidance.md))*

**device-synchronized timing**: timing in which the clock stops only after the device has finished the work being timed, either by the host waiting for it or by reading timestamps the device wrote itself; a clock stopped when the call returns reads the host's cost of handing over the work. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**differentiation rules**: the short list (constants and multiples, sums, products, quotients, powers) from which the derivative of any formula built from simple pieces is computed without returning to the limit. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**diffusion restoration**: restoration by running a diffusion sampler from noise while conditioning every step on the degraded picture, so that the output is a draw from the model's distribution of pictures consistent with the input and not their mean. *([Restoration and Super-Resolution](v08-image-generation/12-restoration.md))*

**diffusion transformer**: a denoiser made of transformer blocks over the patch tokens of a latent, with the noise level entering through adaptive layer normalization, and a last layer that maps the tokens back to patches. *([Denoiser Architectures: U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers](v08-image-generation/08-denoiser-architectures.md))*

**directional derivative**: the rate of change of a function per unit distance in a chosen unit direction $\mathbf{u}$, equal to $\nabla L\cdot\mathbf{u}$. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**discrete Fourier transform**: the list $X[k] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n]e^{-2\pi i kn/N}$ of correlations of $N$ samples with turning pointers, one per frequency $k$; its modulus gives the amplitude and its angle the phase of the component at that frequency, and the original samples are recovered by the inverse transform. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**discriminator**: a classifier trained to tell real samples from a generator's samples, whose output is the probability that a sample is real; at its best it equals $p/(p + q)$. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**disparity**: the reciprocal of depth, $1/Z$, called disparity when it is measured as the shift between the two pictures of a stereo pair; it is the coordinate in which depth varies smoothly and in which a scale and shift ambiguity is linear. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**distribution focal loss**: the cross-entropy between the softmax over the bins of one box side and the two-hot distribution on the two bins around the true distance, which is minimized by that distribution (whose expectation is the true distance) and so constrains the shape and not only the mean. *([Object Detection](v07-vision/04-detection.md))*

**distribution shift**: a difference between the source of the rows a model will meet and the source of the rows it was fitted to and scored on, which no held-out set from the training source can reveal. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**distributional hypothesis**: the idea that tokens occurring in similar contexts have similar meanings, so a model trained to predict from context gives such tokens similar vectors. *([Embeddings](v05-sequences/03-embeddings.md))*

**document layout**: the two-dimensional arrangement of a page's content, columns, lines, tables and their order of reading, which a model must carry from a grid of pixels into a sequence of rows and back out as an ordered transcript. *([Reading Documents](v07-vision/10-ocr.md))*

**dot product**: the number $\sum_i a_i b_i$ obtained from two vectors of equal length, equal to $\lVert\mathbf{a}\rVert\lVert\mathbf{b}\rVert\cos\theta$. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**dropout**: randomly setting each unit of a layer to zero with probability $p_{\mathrm{drop}}$ during training, and scaling the kept units by $1/(1 - p_{\mathrm{drop}})$ so that the expected output is unchanged; the layer is the identity at prediction time. *([Regularization in Neural Networks](v03-neural-networks/11-regularization.md))*

**dynamic resolution**: letting the grid of a picture, and so its number of tokens, follow its size and shape instead of resizing every picture to one fixed square: each side is rounded to a multiple of the patch times the merge, and the area is bounded from both ends. *([Vision-Language Models](v07-vision/09-vlms.md))*

## E

**early stopping**: evaluating the validation loss at intervals, keeping the parameters of the lowest value seen, and stopping when it has not improved for a number of evaluations (the patience). *([Regularization in Neural Networks](v03-neural-networks/11-regularization.md))*

**effect size**: the size of a difference in the metric's own units (points of accuracy), or standardised as the mean difference over the standard deviation of the differences; it says how much a result matters, where a test says only whether chance could explain it. *([Experiments, Baselines and Claims](v02-learning/08-experiments.md))*

**eigenvalue**: the number $\lambda$ by which a matrix stretches one of its eigenvectors, $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}$; the roots of $\det(\mathbf{A} - \lambda\mathbf{I}) = 0$. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**eigenvector**: a nonzero vector that a matrix sends to a multiple of itself, so that the map only stretches (or flips) it. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**embedding gradient**: the gradient of the loss with respect to the table: each row is the sum of the gradient rows of the positions that looked it up, so a token used twice receives two contributions added and a token not used receives exactly zero. *([Embeddings](v05-sequences/03-embeddings.md))*

**embedding table**: the array of shape $[V, D]$ with one row for each token of the vocabulary; looking up a token id returns its row, which is the vector the model computes with, and the rows are learned parameters. *([Embeddings](v05-sequences/03-embeddings.md))*

**encoder-decoder**: a model made of two networks trained together, an encoder that reads an input sequence into states and a decoder that writes an output sequence from them, so that the output may have a different length from the input. *([Encoder-Decoder Models and the Birth of Attention](v05-sequences/06-seq2seq.md))*

**encoder-decoder CNN**: a convolutional network that shrinks the picture to gather context (the encoder) and then enlarges the result back to the picture's resolution (the decoder), usually joined by skip connections that carry high-resolution encoder features to the decoder. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**end-to-end-training-loop**: the whole path from data to saved model in one function: shuffle, batch, forward, loss, backward, clip, optimizer step at the scheduled rate, log, evaluate on the validation set, keep the best checkpoint. *([First Complete Models](v03-neural-networks/13-first-models.md))*

**ensemble**: a set of models whose predictions are combined by a vote or an average; trained independently on resampled data (bagging, random forests) it lowers variance, trained in sequence on what is left (boosting) it lowers bias. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**entropy**: the expected surprise of a distribution, $H(p) = -\sum_k p_k \log p_k$; it is $0$ for a certain outcome, at most $\log K$ for $K$ outcomes, and the lower bound on the average length of a code for data from the distribution. *([Information, Entropy and Surprise](v01-mathematics/13-information-theory.md))*

**epipolar geometry**: the constraint that two views of one scene impose on each other: the image of a point in one view lies on a line, the epipolar line, in the other, expressed for calibrated cameras by $\mathbf{x}_2^\top\mathbf{E}\mathbf{x}_1 = 0$ with the essential matrix $\mathbf{E} = [\mathbf{t}]_\times\mathbf{R}$. *([Structure from Motion and Multi-View Stereo](v10-video-and-3d/04-structure-from-motion.md))*

**epsilon prediction**: asking the network for the noise that was added to the clean value, so that its output $\varepsilon_\theta$ is the estimate from which the clean value or the score follows. *([Diffusion Models](v08-image-generation/05-diffusion.md))*

**equal error rate**: the common value of the false acceptance rate and the false rejection rate at the threshold where the two cross, one number for a model and a set of recordings that says nothing of the cost of either error. *([Who Is Speaking](v09-audio/05-speaker-embeddings.md))*

**estimator**: a rule that turns a sample into a number meant to approximate a quantity of the underlying world; because the sample is random, the number is a random variable with its own distribution, judged by its bias and spread. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**Euler's formula**: the identity $e^{it} = \cos t + i\sin t$, which names the point of the unit circle at angle $t$ and turns the law of exponents into the addition of angles. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**Euler's method**: the rule $x_{i+1} = x_i + h\,f(t_i, x_i)$ that follows the slope of an ODE for a short step $h$ and repeats; with a gradient as the slope it is gradient descent. *([Integrals and Differential Equations](v01-mathematics/09-integrals-and-odes.md))*

**evidence lower bound (ELBO)**: for any distribution $r(z \mid \mathbf{x})$ over the latent, the quantity $\mathbb{E}_r[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x} \mid z)] - D_{\mathrm{KL}}(r \,\Vert\, p(z))$; it is never above the log-likelihood of the reading, and the gap is the KL divergence from $r$ to the model's posterior. *([Variational Autoencoders](v08-image-generation/02-vae.md))*

**exact match**: the share of test questions whose generated answer equals the single reference answer as a string, after a stated normalization; all or nothing, with no partial credit. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**expectation**: the probability-weighted average $\sum_x x\,p(x)$ (or $\int x f(x)\,dx$) of a random variable, the value its long-run average approaches; it is linear, $\mathbb{E}[X + Y] = \mathbb{E}[X] + \mathbb{E}[Y]$. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**expectation-maximization**: the procedure that fits a latent-variable model by repeating one pass in two halves: compute, for every training example, the posterior probability of each value of the latent under the current parameters (the expectation), then replace the parameters by the posterior-weighted averages that the counting formulas would give if the latent had been observed (the maximization); the training likelihood never falls from one pass to the next. *([What It Means to Generate](v08-image-generation/01-generative-modeling.md))*

**expert**: one of several feed-forward networks of the same shape inside a layer, each used only by the tokens that are routed to it; the word does not say what it knows. *([Mixture of Experts](v06-language-models/04-mixture-of-experts.md))*

**expert parallelism**: placing different experts of a layer on different devices, so that tokens are exchanged between devices by an all-to-all to reach their experts and returned with the results. *([Mixture of Experts](v06-language-models/04-mixture-of-experts.md))*

**exploding-gradient**: the same product with factors above one, so that the gradient grows geometrically toward the early layers and a step on them is enormous. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**exponent**: the count of repeated factors in $b^n$, extended to zero, negative and fractional counts by the rule $b^m b^n = b^{m+n}$. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**exponential function**: a function $b^x$ that multiplies by the same factor for each unit step in $x$, growing if $b > 1$ and decaying if $b < 1$. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

## F

**F1 score**: the harmonic mean of precision and recall, $2PR/(P + R) = 2\mathrm{TP}/(2\mathrm{TP} + \mathrm{FP} + \mathrm{FN})$, a single number that is near $0$ when either is. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**face detection**: finding every face in a photograph as a box with a confidence and five landmark points, so that each face can be aligned to a template; a detector of one class that carries an extra output. *([Faces: Detection, Identity and Parsing](v07-vision/11-faces.md))*

**face parsing**: semantic segmentation of a face crop into the parts of a head and its surroundings, with a fixed set of classes, one for every pixel. *([Faces: Detection, Identity and Parsing](v07-vision/11-faces.md))*

**fast Fourier transform**: an algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform that splits the samples into even and odd indices and combines the two half-size transforms with one twiddle multiplication per output pair, using about $\tfrac N2\log_2 N$ multiplications instead of $N^2$ and giving the same result up to rounding. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**feature**: one measurable property of an example that a prediction may depend on; the features of one example form a vector. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**feature matching**: pairing the keypoints of two images by the similarity of their descriptors, usually by the nearest neighbour under a ratio test and a mutual test, so that the pairs are views of the same scene point. *([Structure from Motion and Multi-View Stereo](v10-video-and-3d/04-structure-from-motion.md))*

**feature pyramid**: a set of maps of the same width at several strides built from a backbone's levels, each coarse level's context upsampled and added to the finer level's projection (top-down) and, in the path aggregation form, the fine level's detail carried back to the coarse ones by strided convolutions (bottom-up), so that every scale has both resolution and meaning. *([Convolutional Networks and Residual Learning](v07-vision/03-cnns.md))*

**feed-forward network**: the sublayer that applies one small network, two or three matrices and an activation, to each position on its own, so that it computes with what attention has gathered and moves nothing between positions. *([The Transformer Block](v05-sequences/09-transformer-block.md))*

**feed-forward reconstruction**: recovering cameras and scene geometry from images by one evaluation of a trained network, with no optimisation over the images at the time of use, in place of the matching, robust estimation and adjustment of structure from motion. *([Learning 3D Directly](v10-video-and-3d/05-feed-forward-3d.md))*

**finite difference**: an estimate of a derivative built from values of the function at nearby points, such as the forward difference $(f(x+h) - f(x))/h$. *([Proving Gradients Correct](v03-neural-networks/06-gradient-checking.md))*

**flash attention**: tiled attention with the online softmax in one fused kernel: exact attention whose only results are the output and one log-sum-exp per row, using memory linear in the sequence length and global-memory traffic of $\Theta(T^2 d_h^2 / M)$ for a fast memory of $M$ numbers. *([Attention Without the Quadratic Memory](v05-sequences/13-flash-attention.md))*

**flash attention backward**: the backward pass of attention that saves only the output and the row log-sum-exp, rebuilds each weight as $e^{s - \mathrm{lse}}$ tile by tile, replaces the row sum of the softmax rule by $D_i = d\mathbf{o}_i \cdot \mathbf{o}_i$, and produces the gradients of the queries, keys and values without storing any $T \times T$ matrix. *([Attention Without the Quadratic Memory](v05-sequences/13-flash-attention.md))*

**floating-point number**: a number stored as a sign, an exponent in a fixed range and a significand of fixed precision $p$ bits, $(-1)^s(1 + f/2^{p-1})2^e$; it keeps the same number of significant digits at every scale, so the absolute gap between neighbours doubles with each binade. *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

**FLOPs per token**: the arithmetic of a forward pass for one token, two FLOPs for every active parameter plus four per layer, query-head width and key seen for the attention products, $2N_{\mathrm{act}} + 4LHd_hT$; a property of the shapes and not of the hardware. *([Counting Parameters, FLOPs and Memory](v06-language-models/10-model-cost.md))*

**flow matching**: training a network to give the velocity field by regressing, with squared error, on the velocity of a sampled pair at its own point of the path; the constant that separates this loss from the loss on the field itself does not depend on the network. *([Flow Matching and Rectified Flow](v08-image-generation/06-flow-matching.md))*

**forward noising process**: the chain that turns a data value into noise by adding a little Gaussian noise at each step, $x_t = \sqrt{1 - \beta_t}\,x_{t-1} + \sqrt{\beta_t}\,\varepsilon_t$, which by the addition of Gaussians gives any step directly from the clean value, $x_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\,x_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar\alpha_t}\,\varepsilon$. *([Diffusion Models](v08-image-generation/05-diffusion.md))*

**forward pass**: computing every value of the computational graph in order, from the inputs to the loss. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**forward-mode differentiation**: computing derivatives by carrying the derivative with respect to one input forward through the graph, which costs one pass per input. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**Fourier residual stream**: a residual stream whose entries are the lowest $m$ coefficients of a real orthonormal Fourier basis of a virtual signal of $D$ samples, never stored in full; a basis change alone is absorbed into a dense model's weights, so it matters only together with operators defined relative to the basis. *([A Research Architecture: The Spectral Language Model](v06-language-models/09-spectral-lm.md))*

**fp16 format**: the 16-bit floating-point layout of 1 sign bit, 5 exponent bits (bias 15) and 10 fraction bits: about 3.3 digits, but a largest finite number of only 65504 and a smallest subnormal of $6 \times 10^{-8}$. *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**fp32 format**: the 32-bit floating-point layout of 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127) and 23 fraction bits, with about 7 decimal digits and a range of 83 decades. *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**fp8 format**: either of the two 8-bit floating-point layouts, E4M3 (4 exponent, 3 fraction bits, no infinity, one NaN pattern, largest finite number 448) and E5M2 (5 exponent, 2 fraction bits, IEEE infinities and NaNs, largest finite number 57344), used with a scale per block of values. *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**frame sequence**: a video as an ordered list of pictures of one size, each shown at its own time, usually at a fixed rate in frames per second. *([Video as Data](v10-video-and-3d/01-video.md))*

**function**: a rule that assigns exactly one output to each input from its domain; the range is the set of outputs that actually occur. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

**function notation**: the writing $f(x)$ for the output of the rule $f$ at the input $x$, and $f(x; w, b)$ to separate inputs from parameters. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**fundamental theorem of calculus**: the rate of change of the accumulated area $\int_a^x f(t)\,dt$ is $f(x)$, so $\int_a^b f = F(b) - F(a)$ for any antiderivative $F$ with $F' = f$. *([Integrals and Differential Equations](v01-mathematics/09-integrals-and-odes.md))*

## G

**gamma encoding**: the fixed nonlinear curve, in sRGB a short line and a power law, that maps linear light to the stored code so that equal steps in the code are roughly equal ratios of light; averaging encoded values is therefore not averaging light. *([Images as Data](v07-vision/01-images.md))*

**gated delta network**: a delta-rule memory whose state is first multiplied by a decay gate chosen by the token, with a write strength chosen the same way, so that it forgets as well as corrects. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**gated linear unit**: a hidden layer whose output is the product of two linear functions of the input, one of them passed through a nonlinearity that acts as a gate, so that each hidden unit can be switched or scaled by a second projection. *([The Transformer Block](v05-sequences/09-transformer-block.md))*

**gating**: multiplying a signal elementwise by a vector of sigmoid outputs, each between 0 and 1 and computed from the current input and state, so that the network decides for each unit and each step how much of the signal passes. *([Recurrent Networks](v05-sequences/05-recurrent-networks.md))*

**Gaussian distribution**: the bell-shaped distribution with density $\frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-(x-\mu)^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, fixed by its mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$, written $\mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$ and also called the normal distribution. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**gelu**: the Gaussian error linear unit $z\,\Phi(z)$, the input times the probability that a standard Gaussian variable lies below it, a smooth cousin of the ReLU that dips slightly below zero for negative inputs; it is computed exactly with the error function or approximately by a tanh form or a sigmoid form that are different functions. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**generative model**: a representation of a probability distribution over data, here over images, that can be sampled to produce new data, evaluated to give the probability or density of a given image, or both. *([What It Means to Generate](v08-image-generation/01-generative-modeling.md))*

**generator network**: a network that maps a noise vector drawn from a simple distribution to a sample, so that the samples it makes are draws from a distribution whose density need not be computable; it is the decoder of an autoencoder with the encoder removed. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**global gradient norm**: the Euclidean norm of the gradient of every parameter of the model, all tensors taken together as one vector, the number a clip compares with its threshold. *([Learning-Rate Schedules and Gradient Clipping](v03-neural-networks/08-schedules-and-clipping.md))*

**GPT architecture**: a decoder-only transformer language model: token embeddings plus positions, a stack of pre-norm blocks, a final normalization and a head (tied to the embedding table in GPT-2) that gives one row of logits per position, trained to predict the next token. *([Training a GPT from Scratch](v05-sequences/10-training-gpt.md))*

**GPU architecture**: the organization of a graphics processor used for computing: many compute units, each with lanes, a large register file, a small on-chip memory and a scheduler, over a memory of high bandwidth and high latency, built for throughput and not for the speed of one thread. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**gradient**: the vector of all the partial derivatives of a scalar function, the same shape as its inputs; it points in the direction of steepest ascent and its length is the steepest rate of change. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**gradient accumulation**: adding each contribution to a value's gradient into one persistent buffer, never assigning, with the buffer zeroed once per optimiser step; it sums the uses of a shared weight and the pieces of a batch split into micro-batches. *([The Backward Pass of Every Layer](v03-neural-networks/05-layer-gradients.md))*

**gradient check**: a test that compares the gradient returned by a backward pass with finite-difference estimates of the same forward pass, entry by entry or along random directions, under a stated step and tolerance. *([Proving Gradients Correct](v03-neural-networks/06-gradient-checking.md))*

**gradient clipping**: multiplying the gradient by $\min(1, \tau_{\mathrm{clip}}/(\lVert\mathbf{g}\rVert + \epsilon_{\mathrm{clip}}))$ so that its length never exceeds a threshold and its direction is kept, as a guard against rare very large gradients. *([Learning-Rate Schedules and Gradient Clipping](v03-neural-networks/08-schedules-and-clipping.md))*

**gradient descent**: the iteration that repeatedly moves the parameters a small step against the gradient of the loss, $\mathbf{w} \leftarrow \mathbf{w} - \eta\nabla\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{w})$. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**graph compiler**: a program that takes a whole graph and produces the program an accelerator runs, by passes that no single kernel can make: fusing operations, choosing layouts, tiling layers to the on-chip buffer, planning memory from tensor lifetimes and emitting the command words. *([Neural Processing Units and Graph Compilers](v04-computation/13-npu.md))*

**graph export**: the one-time conversion of a model's forward computation into a static dataflow graph, with every operation a node of a known type, every tensor of a fixed shape and every constant stored in the graph, so that a compiler or device can run it without any of the model's own code. *([Neural Processing Units and Graph Compilers](v04-computation/13-npu.md))*

**greedy decoding**: choosing, at every step, the token of largest probability (the first on a tie), so that the text is a deterministic function of the model and the prompt and, for a model that reads a bounded window, eventually repeats. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**group-normalization**: normalizing groups of consecutive channels of one example, over the group's channels and all spatial positions, with a learned gain and shift per channel; one group is layer normalization and one group per channel is instance normalization. *([Normalization Layers](v03-neural-networks/10-normalization.md))*

**group-wise quantization**: giving each run of $G$ consecutive weights its own scale, so that one large weight sets the step for its group only; it costs $(\text{scale bits})/G$ bits per weight in addition to the codes. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**grouped-query attention**: attention in which each key-value head is read by a group of neighbouring query heads, so a layer stores $h_{\mathrm{kv}}$ key-value heads for $H$ query heads, the cache is $h_{\mathrm{kv}} / H$ of the multi-head cache, and the attention FLOPs are unchanged. *([Anatomy of a Modern Decoder](v06-language-models/01-modern-decoder.md))*

**gru**: gated recurrent unit, a recurrent cell with one state, an update gate that sets how far the state moves toward a new candidate and a reset gate that sets how much of the old state the candidate may read, so that the old state reaches the new one through a gate and not through a matrix. *([Recurrent Networks](v05-sequences/05-recurrent-networks.md))*

**guidance distillation**: training a student network by regression on the guided prediction of a teacher, optionally with the guidance scale as an input, so that one pass of the student gives what two passes of the teacher gave. *([Samplers and Guidance](v08-image-generation/07-samplers-and-guidance.md))*

## H

**hashing**: computing from a value, by a fixed rule, a fixed-size number used as the address of the value in a table (giving expected constant-time lookup when the rule spreads the keys) or as a fingerprint that changes if any byte of the value changes. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**he-initialization**: drawing the weights of a ReLU layer with variance $2/n_{\mathrm{in}}$, the factor 2 compensating for the ReLU zeroing half of the second moment. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

**Hessian**: the symmetric matrix of second partial derivatives of a scalar function; $\mathbf{u}^\top\mathbf{H}\mathbf{u}$ is the curvature along the unit direction $\mathbf{u}$. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**hidden layer**: a layer of units between the input and the output whose values are not given by the data; it computes a new description of the input from which the next layer can compute the answer with a simpler rule. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**hierarchical vision transformer**: a vision transformer arranged as a pyramid of stages, in which merging neighbouring patches between stages reduces the number of tokens and widens the channels, like the stages of a convolutional network. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**homogeneous coordinates**: a representation of a point by one more number than it has coordinates, defined up to a nonzero factor, in which a division by depth, a translation and a point at infinity become matrix products. *([Cameras and Projective Geometry](v10-video-and-3d/03-camera-geometry.md))*

**hybrid architecture**: a stack that interleaves a few full-attention layers, whose cache grows with the context, with many layers of a fixed-size recurrence or convolution, whose cost does not. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**hypothesis space**: the set of all functions a model can express as its parameters vary. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**hypothesis test**: a rule for deciding whether data are consistent with a claim that nothing is going on (the null hypothesis), by computing the probability, assuming the claim, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed (the p-value) and comparing it with a threshold fixed in advance. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

## I

**identity adapter**: the weights added to a frozen generator to condition it on who a person is: a resampler that turns an identity embedding into a few tokens, and at each attention site its own key and value projections for them. *([Control, Identity and Adapters](v08-image-generation/11-control-and-identity.md))*

**identity embedding**: a vector computed from a photograph of a person so that photographs of the same person point the same way and photographs of different people do not; two of them are compared by the cosine of the angle between them. *([Faces: Detection, Identity and Parsing](v07-vision/11-faces.md))*

**identity matrix**: the square matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere, which leaves every vector unchanged. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**im2col**: the unrolling of an image into a matrix with one row per window position, so that a convolution becomes one matrix product with the weights, at the price of a matrix about $k^2$ times the input in size. *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**image generation pipeline**: the sequence of stages that turns a request into an image (text encoding, optional reference encoding, the sampled denoising loop and the decode) together with the contracts between them: shapes, latent scale and packing, row order and position ids, schedule, randomness, and which weights are on which device when. *([Latent Diffusion Systems End to End](v08-image-generation/10-latent-diffusion-systems.md))*

**image resampling**: computing an image of a new size by looking up each output pixel at a source coordinate fixed by a convention (half-pixel, corner-aligned or asymmetric) and combining nearby source pixels with a kernel that is widened when the image shrinks. *([Images as Data](v07-vision/01-images.md))*

**image token splicing**: replacing, in the embedding rows of a prompt, the rows at the placeholder ids by the projector's rows computed from a picture, in order, with a backward pass that carries their gradient to the projector and zeroes them where they were. *([Vision-Language Models](v07-vision/09-vlms.md))*

**implementation candidate**: one implementation of an operation together with the conditions under which it is valid (the capabilities it needs, the shapes it serves, the contract of its result), one of several that a selector chooses among. *([Choosing the Fastest Correct Kernel](v04-computation/10-kernel-selection.md))*

**independence**: the property that $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$, so that knowing one event tells nothing about the other; it is not the same as being unable to occur together. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**inference memory formula**: the sum that bounds what a loaded model holds: the weights at their bytes per parameter, the cache summed over layers with each layer's window, the scratch of one forward pass over a chunk of rows, and an overhead for the allocator and the driver. *([Counting Parameters, FLOPs and Memory](v06-language-models/10-model-cost.md))*

**InfoNCE**: the loss that scores each positive pair by a softmax cross-entropy against the negatives of the batch, written here in its symmetric form (rows and columns of the matrix of cosines times a logit scale), which also lower-bounds the shared information by the logarithm of the batch size minus the loss. *([Contrastive Vision-Language Learning](v07-vision/08-clip.md))*

**information content**: the surprise of an event, $-\log_2 p$ bits (or $-\ln p$ nats) for an event of probability $p$, the only measure for which certain events carry zero, rarer events carry more and independent events add. *([Information, Entropy and Surprise](v01-mathematics/13-information-theory.md))*

**input normalization**: subtracting a per-channel mean and dividing by a per-channel standard deviation, with exactly the constants and channel order the model was trained with, before the first layer. *([Images as Data](v07-vision/01-images.md))*

**integer**: a whole number, positive, negative or zero, with no fractional part; the exact numbers of counting and naming. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**integer-quantized format**: a storage format that keeps each number as a small integer code (8 or 4 bits) and recovers it as a shared scale times the code (less a zero point where the range is not symmetric). *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*
