**integral**: the limit of the Riemann sums $\sum f(t_i)\,\Delta t$ as the width goes to zero, written $\int_a^b f(t)\,dt$; the signed area between the graph of $f$ and the axis. *([Integrals and Differential Equations](v01-mathematics/09-integrals-and-odes.md))*

**intersection over union**: the area two boxes share divided by the area they cover together, a number from 0 to 1 that is unchanged by scaling or shifting both boxes and is 0 for boxes that do not meet. *([Object Detection](v07-vision/04-detection.md))*

**inverse function**: the function $f^{-1}$ that undoes $f$, so $f^{-1}(f(x)) = x$; it exists when $f$ is one-to-one. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

## J

**Jacobian**: the matrix of shape outputs by inputs whose entry $(i, j)$ is $\partial f_i/\partial x_j$; it is the best linear approximation of a vector function near a point. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**Jensen-Shannon divergence**: the symmetric measure of the difference between two distributions p and q, the mean of the KL divergences of p and of q from their mixture, which is zero when they are equal and never more than log 2; it is the value of the adversarial game, up to a constant, at the best discriminator. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**JIT compilation**: compiling a kernel to machine code at the moment a program needs it, on the machine that runs it, so that it fits the device present; the work of the compiler is paid at run time, usually saved in a cache. *([One Program, Many Devices](v04-computation/09-backends.md))*

**joint attention**: one attention in which the prompt tokens and the image tokens are queries and keys of the same softmax, so that each kind of token is updated by the other; a diffusion transformer built on it keeps the prompt as part of its sequence. *([Denoiser Architectures: U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers](v08-image-generation/08-denoiser-architectures.md))*

**joint audio-video generation**: one transformer that denoises a video latent and an audio latent together, each in a stream of its own, coupled in every block by cross-attention in both directions on a shared clock of seconds. *([Generating Video](v10-video-and-3d/02-video-generation.md))*

**joint distribution**: the probability $p(x, y)$ of each pair of values of two random variables on the same experiment, whose row and column sums are the marginal distributions. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

## K

**k-means**: the method that finds $k$ group centres by alternately assigning each row to its nearest centre and moving each centre to the mean of its rows (Lloyd's algorithm), lowering the total squared distance to the centres at every step. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**k-nearest neighbours**: a classifier that stores the training rows and predicts the most common label among the $k$ rows nearest to a new one; $k$ trades bias against variance. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**k-quantization**: a family of block formats in which a super-block of weights is divided into sub-blocks whose scales and mins are themselves stored as small integers times one or two shared factors (two levels of scale), as in Q4_K: 256 weights, eight sub-blocks, 144 bytes. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**kernel dispatch**: the host-side act of running a kernel: binding buffers to its slots, writing its uniform parameters and enqueueing it over a grid of workgroups, after which the host may continue while the device runs it. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**kernel fusion**: replacing a chain of kernels, each consuming what the one before produced, by one kernel that computes the whole chain and keeps the intermediate results in registers or shared memory instead of writing them to buffers and reading them back. *([Kernel Fusion and Memory Traffic](v04-computation/08-fusion.md))*

**kernel method**: a method that fits a linear model on a (possibly enormous) feature map of the inputs while computing only the kernel, the dot product of the features of two rows, as in kernel ridge regression and the support vector machine. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**kernel size, stride and padding**: the side of the window, the number of pixels it moves between neighbouring outputs, and the border of zeros added around the image; with the dilation, which spaces the taps, they fix the output size $\lfloor (H + 2p - d(k-1) - 1)/s \rfloor + 1$. *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**KL divergence**: the excess of the cross-entropy over the entropy, $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p \,\Vert\, q) = \sum_k p_k \log(p_k/q_k)$; it is never negative, zero only when $q = p$, and not symmetric in its arguments. *([Information, Entropy and Surprise](v01-mathematics/13-information-theory.md))*

**KV cache**: for every layer, the key and the value of every token already seen, stored once and read by every later token, so that the past is never run through the model again; its size is two rows of $h_{\mathrm{kv}} d_h$ numbers per token and layer. *([The KV Cache](v05-sequences/12-kv-cache.md))*

**KV offload**: keeping part of the key-value cache in host memory and moving it back to the device when it is needed; because a decoded sequence reads all its cache at every token, what pays is moving whole sequences between scheduling turns, which raises how many sequences can be admitted and not how long one running sequence can be. *([Long Context](v06-language-models/08-long-context.md))*

## L

**L1 regularization**: adding to the loss a penalty proportional to the sum of the absolute values of the weights, which is the effect of a Laplace prior and sets some weights exactly to zero. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**L2 regularization**: adding to the loss a penalty proportional to the sum of the squared weights, which is the effect of a Gaussian prior on the weights and shrinks them smoothly toward zero. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**label**: the answer attached to an example, the quantity a supervised model is asked to predict. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**label-smoothing**: replacing the one-hot target by a mixture of it with the uniform distribution, so that the loss is smallest at a finite gap between the scores instead of only in the limit of infinite confidence. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**latent diffusion**: running the iterated denoiser in the compressed latent space of an autoencoder that was trained earlier and is frozen at generation time, so that the full-resolution decoder runs once at the end and not at every step. *([Latent Diffusion Systems End to End](v08-image-generation/10-latent-diffusion-systems.md))*

**latent space**: the space of codes of a latent-variable model together with its prior and its maps, an encoder into it and a decoder out of it that is defined and trained at every point the prior can produce; nearby codes decode to similar readings, and a typical draw from the prior decodes to a plausible one. *([Variational Autoencoders](v08-image-generation/02-vae.md))*

**latent sparse attention**: selecting keys by scoring buckets of keys in a low-dimensional unit-length index space, reading the members of the best buckets together with the most recent keys and the first few, so that the scoring work grows with the number of buckets and not the number of keys. *([Sparse Attention](v06-language-models/06-sparse-attention.md))*

**latent variable**: a variable that is part of a model but never observed, whose value is a hidden cause of the data; the model's density sums or integrates it out. *([What It Means to Generate](v08-image-generation/01-generative-modeling.md))*

**launch overhead**: the fixed cost of starting work on a device, paid per submission and per dispatch regardless of how much the kernel does, which makes many tiny kernels cost mostly their starts. *([Kernel Fusion and Memory Traffic](v04-computation/08-fusion.md))*

**law of large numbers**: the statement that the average of $n$ independent draws with finite variance converges to their expectation, with the probability of an error above any fixed amount going to zero as $n$ grows. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**layer-normalization**: normalizing each example's features with the mean and variance taken over the features of that one example, then applying a learned gain and shift; it does not depend on the batch or the mode. *([Normalization Layers](v03-neural-networks/10-normalization.md))*

**learned index selection**: choosing the keys a query reads by ranking all keys with a second, cheaper scorer (the indexer) and attending exactly to the top few; the scorer is trained to imitate the dense attention because the ranking itself has no gradient. *([Sparse Attention](v06-language-models/06-sparse-attention.md))*

**learned-controller**: a network trained to produce a control command from the state of a system, here by imitating the commands of a classical controller, and judged by the behaviour of the system when it is in charge. *([First Complete Models](v03-neural-networks/13-first-models.md))*

**learning rate**: the positive number $\eta$ that scales the step of gradient descent; too small is slow, above $2/\lambda_{\max}$ the iteration diverges on a quadratic loss. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**learning-rate warmup**: a learning rate that rises from a small value to its peak over the first $W$ steps, $\eta_t = \eta_{\max}(t+1)/W$, so that the first updates of an adaptive optimizer, whose averages are not yet calibrated, are small. *([Learning-Rate Schedules and Gradient Clipping](v03-neural-networks/08-schedules-and-clipping.md))*

**least squares**: the method of choosing parameters that minimise the sum of the squared differences between predictions and labels. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**lens distortion**: the departure of a real lens from the pinhole, modelled as a correction of the normalized image point (a radial polynomial and tangential terms) or as a polynomial in the angle of the ray, valid only where the polynomial still increases with the distance from the axis. *([Cameras and Projective Geometry](v10-video-and-3d/03-camera-geometry.md))*

**likelihood**: the probability (or density) that a model with a given parameter assigns to the observed data, read as a function of the parameter; it is not the probability of the parameter. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**limit**: the value a quantity approaches as its input gets close to a point without reaching it; $\lim_{h\to 0} g(h) = L$ means $g(h)$ can be made as close to $L$ as we like by taking $h$ small enough and nonzero. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**linear attention**: attention whose scores are used without a softmax, so that the output is $\mathbf{S}_i^\top\mathbf{q}_i$ for a matrix state $\mathbf{S}_i = \sum_{j \le i}\mathbf{k}_j\mathbf{v}_j^\top$ that is updated by one outer product per token and has a fixed size. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**linear map**: a function of vectors that commutes with addition and scaling, and is determined by what it does to the unit vectors. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**linear separability**: the property of labelled points that some line (plane, flat sheet) puts all points of one class on one side and all points of the other on the other; equivalently, the labelling is computed by a single threshold neuron. *([The Neuron and the Perceptron](v03-neural-networks/01-perceptron.md))*

**Lion**: an update that steps by exactly the learning rate in the sign of an interpolation of the momentum and the new gradient, keeping one state array instead of Adam's two. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**load balancing**: any way of making the experts receive about equal numbers of tokens, by an added loss on the router's probabilities or by a selection bias moved with the observed load. *([Mixture of Experts](v06-language-models/04-mixture-of-experts.md))*

**log-mel spectrogram**: the array of mel energies of every frame after a logarithm with a guard or a floor, the input of most speech models. *([Spectrograms and the Mel Scale](v09-audio/02-spectrograms.md))*

**log-probabilities**: the logarithms of probabilities, at most 0, which a decoder reports and adds instead of multiplying probabilities, each stated for the distribution it belongs to: the model's or the sampler's. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**log-sum-exp**: the function $\log \sum_i e^{z_i}$, computed stably as $m + \log \sum_i e^{z_i - m}$ with $m = \max_i z_i$ so that no exponential overflows and the sum is at least $1$; it is the logarithm of a sum of probabilities given their logarithms, and the denominator of the log of a softmax. *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

**logarithm**: the exponent to which a base must be raised to give a number; it is the inverse of the exponent and turns a product into a sum, $\log(uv) = \log u + \log v$. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**logit**: the logarithm of the odds of an event, $\log\frac{p}{1-p}$, a number on the whole real line that a weighted sum of features can model; the model's $z = \mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{x}$ is the logit of its predicted probability. *([Classification and Logistic Regression](v02-learning/03-logistic-regression.md))*

**long-form audio generation**: the production of audio longer than any one component can attend to at once, by generating it in overlapping windows, each started from the end of the last, and cropping and joining the results. *([Music Generation](v09-audio/07-music.md))*

**looped transformer**: a transformer whose block, or whole stack of blocks, is applied repeatedly to its own output a fixed number of times, with the embedding applied once at the start and the head reading the final state. *([Looped and Recurrent-Depth Transformers](v06-language-models/07-recurrent-depth.md))*

**loss curve**: the loss plotted against the training step or epoch; it can show the minibatch loss, the loss on the whole training set or on a validation set, each with a different noise level and cost, and it is read by its start, direction, slope and gap. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**loss function**: a rule that scores one prediction against its label with a non-negative number, zero for a perfect prediction; its average over the data is the quantity learning minimises. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**loss masking**: giving every position a mask of 1 or 0, so that padding and prompt tokens are computed but contribute nothing to the loss or the gradient, and dividing by the count of positions with mask 1 and not by the size of the batch. *([Training a GPT from Scratch](v05-sequences/10-training-gpt.md))*

**low-rank approximation**: replacing a matrix by one of small rank, best obtained by keeping the largest singular values; it stores $r(m + n)$ numbers instead of $mn$ and its error is the dropped singular values. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**lstm**: long short-term memory, a recurrent cell with a cell state that is kept by a forget gate and added to by an input gate and shown through an output gate, so that the gradient has a path along the cell state with no weight matrix and no slope of the activation. *([Recurrent Networks](v05-sequences/05-recurrent-networks.md))*

## M

**machine epsilon**: the gap between $1$ and the next larger floating-point number, $2^{1-p}$ ($1.19 \times 10^{-7}$ in 32 bits, $2.22 \times 10^{-16}$ in 64 bits); twice the unit round-off $u = 2^{-p}$, which is the bound on the relative error of one rounding. *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

**mask decoder**: the small network that turns the prompt tokens and the stored image embedding into mask logits, by letting tokens and image cells attend to each other and then taking, for each output token, a dot product with the upscaled cells. *([Promptable Segmentation and Video Tracking](v07-vision/07-segment-anything.md))*

**masked language modeling**: the training task of an encoder in which a random subset of positions is selected, the input there is replaced (by a mask token, a random token or nothing, in the proportions 80, 10 and 10 percent), and the model is trained to recover the original tokens at the selected positions only, from both sides. *([Bidirectional Encoders and Embedding Models](v05-sequences/14-encoders.md))*

**matrix**: a table of numbers with $m$ rows and $n$ columns, which is also a linear map from $n$ numbers to $m$ numbers. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**matrix inverse**: the matrix $\mathbf{A}^{-1}$ that undoes $\mathbf{A}$, so $\mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{A}$ is the identity; it exists only for a square matrix whose rank equals its size. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**matrix multiplication**: the matrix of the composition of two linear maps, $(\mathbf{B}\mathbf{A})_{ij} = \sum_l B_{il}A_{lj}$, defined when the inner sizes agree. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**matrix-vector product**: the vector whose entries are the dot products of the rows of a matrix with the input vector, equivalently a weighted sum of the matrix's columns. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**maximum a posteriori**: choosing the parameter at the peak of the posterior, equivalently minimising the negative log-likelihood plus the negative log of the prior. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**maximum likelihood estimation**: choosing the parameter under which the observed data were most probable, equivalently the one that minimises the negative log-likelihood. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**mean squared error**: the average over the examples of the squared difference between prediction and label, $\frac{1}{N}\sum_n (\hat{y}_n - y_n)^2$. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**measured roofline**: the peak arithmetic rate and the memory bandwidth of the device itself, found by two probes that do nothing but arithmetic and nothing but streaming and whose work is counted, in whose terms every result is stated as a fraction. *([Choosing the Fastest Correct Kernel](v04-computation/10-kernel-selection.md))*

**mel filterbank**: a set of overlapping triangular weights whose edges are equally spaced on the mel scale, which turns a spectrum into one energy for each band. *([Spectrograms and the Mel Scale](v09-audio/02-spectrograms.md))*

**mel scale**: a function from frequency to pitch, nearly linear below 1000 Hz and logarithmic above, fitted to listening experiments, in an HTK form and a Slaney form. *([Spectrograms and the Mel Scale](v09-audio/02-spectrograms.md))*

**memory attention**: the attention of a video frame's features onto a bank of memories of earlier frames and object pointers, with position encoded by rotation, which marks the cells that resemble the tracked object before the mask is decoded. *([Promptable Segmentation and Video Tracking](v07-vision/07-segment-anything.md))*

**memory bandwidth**: the number of bytes per second that main memory can deliver to the processor when the program asks for them in the best possible way (long sequential reads), a property of the machine and not of the program. *([Memory Bandwidth, Compute and the Roofline](v04-computation/03-roofline.md))*

**memory coalescing**: the merging of the loads or stores of the lanes of a subgroup into few memory transactions when they touch adjacent addresses, so that all the bytes of each block moved are used. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**memory complexity**: the amount of memory, counted in cells and measured at the peak, that an algorithm needs as a function of its input size; it can be traded against time by storing a result instead of recomputing it, or the reverse. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**memory-traffic accounting**: the routine of listing for every kernel of a program the FLOPs it executes and the distinct bytes it reads and writes, each operand counted once, so that designs of the same computation can be compared by bytes and by arithmetic intensity before anything is run. *([Kernel Fusion and Memory Traffic](v04-computation/08-fusion.md))*

**metric selection**: choosing the number that scores a model from the decision its output feeds and the costs of its mistakes, checking it on a trivial and a perfect predictor, and reporting it with an uncertainty. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**minibatch**: the small set of $B$ examples whose mean loss gradient is used for one update; its gradient has the full gradient's expectation and a variance $1/B$ that of one example. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**mixed-precision weight search**: choosing the storage width of each tensor so as to minimize the estimated total loss increase within a byte budget, using each tensor's sensitivity; a knapsack problem solved greedily and accepted only after measuring the whole model. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**mode collapse**: the failure in which a generator maps most of its noise to a few outputs, so its samples cover only a small part of the data's distribution even if each looks plausible. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**model**: a function whose rule has a fixed shape and whose behaviour is set by a list of parameters, used to turn the features of an example into a prediction. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**modern decoder recipe**: the combination of choices common to present-day open-weight decoders: pre-norm blocks with RMS normalization and no biases, rotary positions applied to normalized queries and keys, grouped key-value heads, a SwiGLU network, and an output matrix that is tied or untied by size. *([Anatomy of a Modern Decoder](v06-language-models/01-modern-decoder.md))*

**momentum**: a running weighted sum of past gradients, $\mathbf{m}_t = \beta\mathbf{m}_{t-1} + \mathbf{g}_t$, stepped along instead of the gradient, so that steady directions add up and back-and-forth directions cancel. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**monocular depth**: estimating the distance of every pixel from a single image; because a picture is unchanged when the world is scaled about the camera, the result is a relative map (up to a scale, and for inverse depth a shift) unless the model has learned the size of things. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**monotonic function**: a function that never reverses direction, always increasing or always decreasing, and so keeps the order of single values. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

**multi-axis rotary embedding**: rotary embedding for tokens that have a position on several axes, such as the frame, row and column of an image patch, in which the channel pairs of a head are divided among the axes and each pair turns by the position on its own axis times its own rate. *([Positional Information](v05-sequences/08-positions.md))*

**multi-head attention**: attention run $H$ times on slices of the width, each head with its own queries, keys and values, the outputs placed side by side and mixed by one output matrix, so that a position can ask several different questions of the same set at once. *([Self-Attention](v05-sequences/07-self-attention.md))*

**multi-latent attention**: attention that computes the keys and values of all heads from one small latent vector per token, caches only the latent and a small rotary key, and absorbs the up-projections into the query and the output at decode time so that no key or value is rebuilt. *([Attention Variants: Sharing and Compressing Keys](v06-language-models/03-attention-variants.md))*

**multi-query attention**: attention in which every query head of a layer reads one shared key and one shared value per position, so a layer caches $2 d_h$ numbers per token instead of $2 H d_h$, and the heads differ only through their queries. *([Attention Variants: Sharing and Compressing Keys](v06-language-models/03-attention-variants.md))*

**multilayer perceptron**: a network of fully connected layers, each followed by an activation function (usually except the last), so that each layer reads all of the outputs of the one before it; the name is historical, since its units rarely use the step. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**multimodal position encoding**: the rule that gives the tokens of a sequence of words and picture rows their positions, such as the index of each row, or a triple of frame, row and column for a patch with a counter that advances past the picture by its largest extent. *([Vision-Language Models](v07-vision/09-vlms.md))*

**multiple comparisons**: the problem that testing many hypotheses makes some significant by chance, so that the chance of at least one false positive grows with their number, controlled by tests at a smaller level such as the Bonferroni correction. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**multivariable chain rule**: the Jacobian of a composition of vector functions is the product of their Jacobians, the outer one evaluated at the inner function's output. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**multivariate Gaussian**: the distribution of a vector $\boldsymbol{\mu} + \mathbf{A}\mathbf{z}$ built from independent standard Gaussians $\mathbf{z}$, fixed by its mean vector and covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{A}^\top$; its level curves are ellipses along the eigenvectors of $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$. *([The Distributions Machine Learning Uses](v01-mathematics/11-distributions.md))*

**music generation**: the production of a long stereo signal from a description of its style and its lyrics by a chain of models that each see a different length of the song, a language model that writes it as codes, a denoiser that paints it as latents and a decoder that turns the latents into samples. *([Music Generation](v09-audio/07-music.md))*

**mutual information**: the divergence of the joint distribution of two variables from the product of their marginals, $I(X; Y) = H(X) - H(X \mid Y)$, the amount by which learning one reduces the uncertainty of the other; it is zero only for independent variables. *([Information, Entropy and Surprise](v01-mathematics/13-information-theory.md))*

## N

**n-gram model**: a language model that estimates the probability of the next token from the last $n - 1$ tokens only, by counting how often each token followed that context in a training text. *([Language Modeling](v05-sequences/04-language-modeling.md))*

**naive Bayes**: a classifier that applies Bayes' rule with the assumption that the features are independent given the class, so that the class probabilities come from simple counts or per-feature distributions. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**naive matmul**: the matrix product computed as its definition reads, one output at a time as a dot product of a row and a column, loading both from memory for every output and keeping nothing between outputs; its intensity is about a quarter of an operation per byte at any size. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**negative log-likelihood**: minus the natural logarithm of the likelihood, a sum over independent examples of the surprise at each observed label; the loss that maximum likelihood minimises. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**neural audio codec**: a trained encoder, quantizer and decoder that turn a waveform into a short sequence of discrete codes and back to a waveform. *([Neural Audio Codecs](v09-audio/03-audio-codecs.md))*

**Newton's method**: the iteration that replaces a function by its tangent line (or, for minimisation, by a quadratic with the same slope and curvature) and jumps to its zero (or bottom), $x \leftarrow x - f(x)/f'(x)$ or $x \leftarrow x - f'(x)/f''(x)$; its error is squared at each step near a simple root. *([Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change](v01-mathematics/07-derivatives.md))*

**next-token prediction**: the training task of giving high probability to each token of a text given the tokens before it, with the mean cross-entropy over all positions as the loss, so that the text supplies its own labels. *([Language Modeling](v05-sequences/04-language-modeling.md))*

**noise schedule**: the rule that fixes how much noise each step adds, given as the variances $\beta_t$, the running products $\bar\alpha_t$ or the signal-to-noise ratios, and in the continuous limit as the rate of a decay equation. *([Diffusion Models](v08-image-generation/05-diffusion.md))*

**non-maximum suppression**: the greedy removal of duplicate detections, visiting candidates by falling confidence and dropping each one whose overlap with an already kept candidate (of its class, unless the suppression is class-agnostic) exceeds a threshold. *([Object Detection](v07-vision/04-detection.md))*

**non-saturating loss**: the generator loss that asks the discriminator to score fakes as real by minimizing -log D on them instead of log(1 - D), whose gradient stays near its largest value exactly when the discriminator is sure a sample is fake and the saturating loss gives none. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**norm**: the length of a vector; the L2 norm is $\sqrt{\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{a}}$, and the L1 and max norms measure total and largest-entry size. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**normal equations**: the system $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\mathbf{w} = \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$ obtained by setting the gradient of the squared error to zero; it says the residual is orthogonal (normal) to every column of the design matrix. *([Linear Regression and the First Descent](v02-learning/02-linear-regression.md))*

**normalization of text**: converting a string to a canonical spelling (NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD) so that strings the standard declares equivalent become identical sequences of code points, before they are compared, counted or tokenized. *([Text as Data](v05-sequences/01-text.md))*

**numerical integration**: approximating an integral by a weighted sum of function values, such as rectangles, trapezoids or Simpson's rule, whose error falls as a fixed power of the panel width. *([Integrals and Differential Equations](v01-mathematics/09-integrals-and-odes.md))*

## O

**occupancy**: the fraction of a compute unit's resident-invocation slots that a kernel fills, limited by the registers per invocation, the shared memory per workgroup, the workgroup size and the cap on resident workgroups. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**ODE solver**: a rule that turns evaluations of a velocity field into the next point of a trajectory, judged by how fast its error falls as the steps shrink (its order) and by how many evaluations of the field each step costs; Euler, Heun and the multistep methods of this chapter are examples. *([Samplers and Guidance](v08-image-generation/07-samplers-and-guidance.md))*

**omni model**: one network whose decoder reads rows from the encoders of several media (sound, pictures, video and text) in a single sequence, and that answers in more than one medium, here in text and in speech. *([Models That Listen, See and Speak](v09-audio/08-omni-models.md))*

**one-hot-encoding**: writing a class index as a vector with a one in the position of that class and zeros elsewhere, the probability vector that puts all its weight on that class. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**online softmax**: the way of computing a softmax and the weighted sum of values in one pass over a row of scores read in chunks, by carrying the running maximum $m$, the running sum $\ell$ of exponentials relative to it and the running weighted sum $\mathbf{o}$, and multiplying the old sum and the old output by $e^{m - m'}$ whenever a chunk raises the maximum from $m$ to $m'$. *([Attention Without the Quadratic Memory](v05-sequences/13-flash-attention.md))*

**ONNX graph**: the interchange form of an exported graph: typed and shaped inputs and outputs, constant tensors (initializers), nodes in an order that defines every input before use, each naming an operator, its inputs, its output and its attributes, and an opset number that fixes the meaning of every operator. *([Neural Processing Units and Graph Compilers](v04-computation/13-npu.md))*

**optical character recognition**: turning the pixels of a page into the characters that were printed on it; in this chapter a decoder writes the page as text while it attends to rows computed from the picture. *([Reading Documents](v07-vision/10-ocr.md))*

**ordinary differential equation**: an equation $dx/dt = f(t, x)$ that gives the rate of change of an unknown function of one variable in terms of the function itself; its solution is a curve that follows the prescribed slopes from a given starting value. *([Integrals and Differential Equations](v01-mathematics/09-integrals-and-odes.md))*

**orthogonal matrix**: a square matrix whose columns are orthonormal, so that $\mathbf{Q}^\top\mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{I}$, its inverse is its transpose, and it preserves lengths and angles. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**orthogonality**: the property of two vectors having dot product 0, that is, being at right angles. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**output stride**: the ratio of the picture's side to the side of the map a network predicts on before any enlargement, so that a stride-4 output holds one prediction per $4 \times 4$ block of pixels. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**overfit-one-batch**: the test of training a network on one fixed small batch for a few hundred steps; the loss must fall to nearly zero, and if it does not the model, loss, data or update is broken. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**overfitting**: a model so flexible for its data that it fits the accidents of the training rows, so that its training error is low and its error on new rows is worse than that of a simpler model. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**overflow and underflow**: overflow is an exact result too large for the format, stored as infinity; underflow is a nonzero result too small, stored with fewer and fewer significant digits (subnormal numbers) and finally as zero. *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

## P

**paged sparse layout**: storing keys and values in fixed-size pages reached through a block table and reading a content-based selection as a list of positions resolved through that table, row by row, without copying the selected rows into one buffer. *([Sparse Attention](v06-language-models/06-sparse-attention.md))*

**paired test**: a comparison of two systems scored on the same examples through the per-example differences, whose standard error is smaller than an unpaired one when the systems' answers are correlated; the paired z-test and the exact sign test are two of them. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**parallel reduction**: a reduction algorithm carried out by many invocations at once, whose cost is described by its work (the operations it performs) and its depth (the longest chain of operations that must wait for one another). *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

**parallel scan**: a prefix sum computed by many invocations in a number of steps that grows with $\log n$, either with $n \log n$ additions (Hillis-Steele) or with $2(n - 1)$ additions and twice the depth (Blelloch), and across workgroups by scanning blocks, scanning their totals and adding the totals back. *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

**parameter**: one of the numbers that set a model's behaviour; fixed while the model predicts and changed while it learns. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**parameter count**: the number of numbers a model stores, the sum over its tensors of the product of their shape; multiplied by the bytes of a format it gives the size of the weights, and it is larger than the number a token's arithmetic uses for a mixture or a model with parameters that are not products. *([Counting Parameters, FLOPs and Memory](v06-language-models/10-model-cost.md))*

**parity tolerance**: the largest difference between two implementations of the same function that rounding alone can explain, derived from the count of roundings along the longest chain of dependent operations times the unit round-off, so that anything above it is evidence of a bug. *([Importing Pretrained Models and Proving Parity](v06-language-models/02-importing-models.md))*

**partial derivative**: the derivative of a function of several variables with respect to one of them while all the others are held fixed, $\partial L/\partial w_j$. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*

**patch discriminator**: a convolutional discriminator whose output is a map of logits, each judging one patch of the image, with the loss averaged over the map, so that it scores texture and local structure and does not tie the network to one image size. *([Adversarial Training](v08-image-generation/04-gans.md))*

**patch embedding**: the layer that turns a picture into a sequence of tokens by cutting it into non-overlapping square patches, flattening each and applying one shared linear map; identical to a convolution whose kernel size equals its stride. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**patch-match stereo**: dense depth estimation in which every pixel holds a plane hypothesis (range and normal), scored by correlation of its patch across views, and a randomized search propagates good hypotheses between neighbouring pixels and refines them, so that a small fraction of the hypothesis space is tried. *([Structure from Motion and Multi-View Stereo](v10-video-and-3d/04-structure-from-motion.md))*

**PCM audio**: pulse-code modulation, a recording stored as integer codes, each the nearest multiple of a fixed step to the waveform at one of equally spaced moments. *([Sound and Sampling](v09-audio/01-sound.md))*

**per-kernel profile**: the table that divides the time of a pass among its dispatches or kernel kinds, with each row's counted FLOPs and bytes, device time, share of the pass and achieved fraction of the device's measured roofline; it explains where the time goes and does not add up to the pass. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**perceptron**: a neuron with a step activation together with Rosenblatt's rule for learning its weights, which adds each misclassified example, signed by its label, to the weights and the bias and repeats over the data until a pass has no mistake. *([The Neuron and the Perceptron](v03-neural-networks/01-perceptron.md))*

**perceptual distance**: a distance (LPIPS, learned perceptual image patch similarity, when the features are learned) between two pictures computed on the features of a pretrained network (channel-normalized at each position, differenced, squared, weighted per channel and averaged over positions and levels), which measures how different they look and need not agree with the pixel error. *([Contrastive Vision-Language Learning](v07-vision/08-clip.md))*

**perceptual loss**: a training loss that is a perceptual distance, the difference of the features that a frozen pretrained network computes for the output and the target, which prefers a sharp output where a squared error prefers the blurred mean. *([Discrete Latents and Vector Quantization](v08-image-generation/03-vector-quantization.md))*

**perplexity**: the exponential of the cross-entropy, $\exp H(p, q)$ with natural logarithms, the number of equally likely choices that would give the same average surprise. *([Information, Entropy and Surprise](v01-mathematics/13-information-theory.md))*

**piecewise function**: a function defined by different rules on different parts of its domain, such as the absolute value, ReLU and a schedule with a warmup. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

**pinhole camera**: the camera that sends each point of the world along a straight ray through one point, the pinhole, to the image, so that the image position is the ratio of the lateral offset to the depth and the depth itself is lost. *([Cameras and Projective Geometry](v10-video-and-3d/03-camera-geometry.md))*

**pixel**: one sample of an image, a point measurement of light (three numbers for a colour image, usually 8-bit codes), taken at the centre of its cell in a grid of width times height. *([Images as Data](v07-vision/01-images.md))*

**pointmap**: an array with one world point per pixel of an image, the point the pixel sees, written in the coordinates of one shared frame (the first camera's), so that a depth map and the camera that took it are one object and two pixels of two images that see the same surface hold the same point. *([Learning 3D Directly](v10-video-and-3d/05-feed-forward-3d.md))*

**polynomial**: a sum of constant multiples of powers of $x$; one of degree $n$ has $n + 1$ parameters and is fixed by $n + 1$ points. *([Functions and Their Shapes](v01-mathematics/02-functions.md))*

**pooled text embedding**: a single vector for the whole prompt, usually the row of an encoder at its end token after the final normalization (and, for SDXL, a projection), with no positions, so that it is added to the timestep embedding and reaches every block with the clock and not through attention. *([Conditioning on Text](v08-image-generation/09-text-conditioning.md))*

**pooling**: a layer that summarizes each window of a map by one number, the largest (max pooling, whose gradient goes to the winner of the window) or the mean (average pooling, whose gradient is shared equally), with no weights; global average pooling takes the whole map. *([Convolutional Networks and Residual Learning](v07-vision/03-cnns.md))*

**post-training quantization**: converting a trained float network to integer arithmetic without retraining, by choosing the scale and zero point of each weight tensor from the weights and of each activation tensor from ranges measured on data, and rewriting each layer as an integer accumulation followed by a requantization. *([Neural Processing Units and Graph Compilers](v04-computation/13-npu.md))*

**pre-norm**: the block layout in which each sublayer reads a normalized copy of the stream and its result is added to the stream unnormalized, $\mathbf{x} + g(\mathrm{norm}(\mathbf{x}))$, so that the path through the additions alone carries no norm. *([The Transformer Block](v05-sequences/09-transformer-block.md))*

**precision and recall**: precision is the share of the examples called positive that are positive, $P(y = 1 \mid \text{decision positive})$; recall is the share of the positive examples that are called positive, $P(\text{decision positive} \mid y = 1)$, also the true positive rate. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**prediction**: the value $\hat{y} = f_\theta(\mathbf{x})$ a model returns for an example. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**prefill phase**: processing the whole prompt in one call, with every matrix seeing all the prompt's rows at once and the keys and values of every prompt position written into the cache; limited by the arithmetic once the prompt is long. *([The KV Cache](v05-sequences/12-kv-cache.md))*

**prefix sum**: the list of running totals of an array, either inclusive (including the element at each position) or exclusive (stopping just before it), used to turn probabilities into a cumulative distribution and lengths into offsets. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**pretokenization**: the fixed split of text into words, digits, symbols and whitespace runs, done before any merge so that merges never cross a boundary; its rules are as much a part of a tokenizer as its vocabulary. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**principal component analysis**: finding the directions along which centred rows vary most, the eigenvectors of their covariance matrix, so that rows can be summarised by their positions along the first few. *([Machine Learning Before Deep Learning](v02-learning/07-classical-methods.md))*

**prior**: a probability distribution over the parameters stating what is believed about them before the data are seen. *([Maximum Likelihood, Priors and Regularization](v02-learning/04-likelihood.md))*

**probability distribution**: the assignment of a probability to each value of a random variable, written as a table for finitely many values or as a density whose area over an interval is the probability. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**probability path**: a family of densities $p_\sigma$, one for each noise fraction, that runs from the data's density at $\sigma = 0$ to the standard normal at $\sigma = 1$; here the density of $x_\sigma = (1 - \sigma)x_0 + \sigma\varepsilon$. *([Flow Matching and Rectified Flow](v08-image-generation/06-flow-matching.md))*

**product notation**: the symbol $\prod_{i=a}^{b} x_i$ for the product of the terms $x_i$ as the index $i$ runs from $a$ to $b$. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**projection**: the closest point to a vector $\mathbf{v}$ on the line through $\mathbf{u}$, namely $\frac{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{u}}{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{u}$; what is left over is orthogonal to $\mathbf{u}$. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**prompt embedding sequence**: the array of rows, one vector per position of the fixed window, that an encoder produces for a prompt, including the rows of the padding; the denoiser reads it by cross-attention or by joint attention. *([Conditioning on Text](v08-image-generation/09-text-conditioning.md))*

**prompt encoder**: the part that turns clicks, box corners and a rough mask into vectors for the decoder: a random Fourier encoding of each coordinate plus a learned embedding of its type, and a convolutional reduction of a mask. *([Promptable Segmentation and Video Tracking](v07-vision/07-segment-anything.md))*

**prompt ensembling**: averaging, for each class, the text vectors of several sentence templates that name it (for example "a photo of a square" and "a drawing of a square") and renormalizing, so that no single template's wording decides the class vector. *([Contrastive Vision-Language Learning](v07-vision/08-clip.md))*

**promptable segmentation**: the task of returning the mask of an object in an image from a prompt, a point, a box or a rough mask, with the same model for every object and no fixed list of classes; a prompt that leaves the extent open is answered with several masks. *([Promptable Segmentation and Video Tracking](v07-vision/07-segment-anything.md))*

**pseudo-random generator**: a deterministic state machine (a state, a rule that advances it, and a rule that turns it into a number) whose outputs are judged by how closely they resemble draws from a uniform distribution, not by being unpredictable to someone who knows the rule. *([Randomness on a Deterministic Machine](v01-mathematics/17-randomness.md))*

## Q

**QK-normalization**: the RMS normalization of every query and every key over its own head width, with a learned gain per channel and applied before the rotary rotation, which bounds attention logits by $\sqrt{d_h}$ times the gains. *([Anatomy of a Modern Decoder](v06-language-models/01-modern-decoder.md))*

**quantization error**: the difference $e = w' - w$ between a decoded weight and the original, bounded by half a step, and summarized by its mean squared error or the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio $10\log_{10}(\mathrm{mean}(w^2)/\mathrm{MSE})$ in decibels. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**query, key and value**: the three vectors that each position's input gives by three separate learned linear maps: the query is what the position asks of the others, the key is what it can be matched on, and the value is what it hands over when matched. *([Self-Attention](v05-sequences/07-self-attention.md))*

## R

**radix sort**: a sort of integer keys digit by digit from the least significant, each pass made of per-chunk histograms, one scan of the digit-major histogram array and a stable scatter, so that no two invocations write the same counter or the same position. *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

**random variable**: a function from the outcomes of an experiment to numbers, such as the number of heads in three flips; the rule is fixed and the randomness is in which outcome occurs. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**rank**: the number of independent columns of a matrix, equal to the number of independent rows and to the dimension of what the map can reach. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**real number**: any number on the number line, including fractions and irrational numbers such as $\sqrt{2}$; a computer holds only an approximation of most of them. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**receptive field**: the set of input pixels on which one output value depends; along one axis its size grows by $d(k-1)$ times the jump (the input distance between neighbouring units) at each layer, and the jump multiplies by the stride. *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**reconstruction-loss**: the mean squared error between an autoencoder's output and its input, $L_{\mathrm{rec}} = \frac{1}{BD}\sum(\hat{x} - x)^2$; it needs no labels. *([First Complete Models](v03-neural-networks/13-first-models.md))*

**rectified flow**: flow matching on the straight path between a data value and a noise value, together with the repetition that pairs data with the noise it was generated from, which straightens the paths until a few Euler steps suffice. *([Flow Matching and Rectified Flow](v08-image-generation/06-flow-matching.md))*

**recurrent depth**: a layout of a prelude that embeds the input once, a core applied a variable number of times to a latent state that starts as noise and re-reads the prelude's output at every step, and a coda that reads out the result, so that the amount of computation is chosen when the model is run. *([Looped and Recurrent-Depth Transformers](v06-language-models/07-recurrent-depth.md))*

**recurrent neural network**: a network that reads a sequence one element at a time, keeping a state of fixed size that is rewritten at every step from its previous value and the current element by the same weights, so that its parameters do not grow with the length of the sequence. *([Recurrent Networks](v05-sequences/05-recurrent-networks.md))*

**reduction algorithm**: an algorithm that combines the elements of an array into one value by repeated use of a binary operation, as a sum, a maximum or an argmax does; it takes $n - 1$ applications, and if the operation is associative they can be regrouped into a tree of depth $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**reference golden**: the stored output of a reference implementation for fixed inputs, with the intermediate activations of every layer, against which an implementation is compared, never committed and always regenerated by a recorded script. *([Importing Pretrained Models and Proving Parity](v06-language-models/02-importing-models.md))*

**reference-gated selection**: choosing among candidates only those whose output on the actual device matches a reference within a tolerance derived from their arithmetic, checked at the edges of the shapes they will serve, before any of them is timed. *([Choosing the Fastest Correct Kernel](v04-computation/10-kernel-selection.md))*

**register blocking**: giving each invocation of a kernel a small square block of outputs held in its registers, so that each operand it reads is used once per row or column of the block, which enlarges the output tile beyond the number of invocations and cuts the reads of shared memory per multiply-add. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**reinforcement learning (overview)**: learning by an agent that acts in an environment and receives rewards, without being told the right action; full treatment in Volume XII. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**rejection sampling**: drawing a candidate from an easy distribution, keeping it only if it passes a test and otherwise drawing again, so that the kept values have the distribution the test selects; it gives unbiased integers and samples from densities with no invertible cumulative distribution, at the cost of the discarded draws. *([Randomness on a Deterministic Machine](v01-mathematics/17-randomness.md))*

**relative error**: the size of the difference between two numbers divided by the larger of their sizes, which is independent of scale but unbounded near zero. *([Proving Gradients Correct](v03-neural-networks/06-gradient-checking.md))*

**relative position**: the offset $j - i$ between a key and a query; a position scheme is relative when the score it produces depends on the two positions only through this offset, whether by rotation, by a learned bias per bucket of offsets or by a fixed slope. *([Positional Information](v05-sequences/08-positions.md))*

**relu**: the rectified linear unit $\max(0, z)$, zero for negative inputs and the identity for positive ones, with slope $1$ where it is positive and $0$ elsewhere. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**reparameterization trick**: writing a draw from a Gaussian as $z = m + \sigma_{\mathrm{q}}\xi$ with a noise $\xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ that does not depend on the parameters, so that the sample is a differentiable function of the mean and the width and the gradient of an expectation is the expectation of a derivative. *([Variational Autoencoders](v08-image-generation/02-vae.md))*

**repetition penalty**: a factor applied to the logits of tokens already in the text, dividing a positive logit and multiplying a negative one, to make repeats less likely; its additive relatives subtract an amount per presence or per occurrence. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**RepMixer**: a convolutional token-mixing block of a hybrid vision encoder, trained with parallel branches and folded at inference into one depthwise $3 \times 3$ convolution, followed by a ConvFFN. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**reporting uncertainty**: stating with a result its intervals over seeds and over the test sample, the numbers of seeds and examples, what was tuned on which split, and how many variants were tried, so that a reader can judge how far to trust it. *([Experiments, Baselines and Claims](v02-learning/08-experiments.md))*

**reproducibility**: the property that running again from the same recorded inputs (seed, data, code, settings) gives the same results exactly, which requires the same draws in the same order and the same floating-point arithmetic. *([Randomness on a Deterministic Machine](v01-mathematics/17-randomness.md))*

**reshape-and-view**: reshaping keeps a tensor's line of numbers in row-major order and cuts it into a new shape; a view is a new shape, strides and offset over the same storage, so a reshape of a contiguous array needs no copy. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**residual network**: a network of blocks that compute $\mathrm{relu}(f(\mathbf{x}) + \mathrm{sh}(\mathbf{x}))$, the sum of a short stack of convolutions and a shortcut (the identity, or a $1 \times 1$ projection when the shape changes), which lets gradients and signals pass a deep stack along a path without weights; the basic block has two $3 \times 3$ convolutions and the bottleneck block a $1 \times 1$ reduction, a $3 \times 3$ and a $1 \times 1$ expansion. *([Convolutional Networks and Residual Learning](v07-vision/03-cnns.md))*

**residual stream**: the matrix of shape $[T, D]$ that enters a transformer block, is added to by each sublayer and leaves it, so that after $L$ blocks it is the embedding plus the $2L$ contributions that the sublayers wrote. *([The Transformer Block](v05-sequences/09-transformer-block.md))*

**residual vector quantization**: a chain of codebooks in which each quantizes the error left by the ones before it, so that the stored indices are one per stage and the reconstruction is the sum of the chosen entries. *([Neural Audio Codecs](v09-audio/03-audio-codecs.md))*

**residual-connection**: a layer that returns its input plus a correction, $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{x} + f(\mathbf{x})$, so that its Jacobian is $\mathbf{I} + \mathbf{J}_f$ and the gradient has a path through it that passes no weights. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**retrieval**: finding the stored texts that answer a query by embedding the query, comparing its vector with the stored vectors and ranking the collection by cosine, judged by the share of the relevant texts found among the top $k$ (recall at $k$). *([Bidirectional Encoders and Embedding Models](v05-sequences/14-encoders.md))*

**reverse-mode differentiation**: computing derivatives by carrying a row vector from the single output back through the chain of Jacobians, so one sweep gives the gradient with respect to every input. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**rms-normalization**: layer normalization without the subtraction of the mean: dividing each example's features by their root mean square and applying a learned gain. *([Normalization Layers](v03-neural-networks/10-normalization.md))*

**RMSProp**: an update that divides each coordinate's gradient by the root of a running average of its own squared gradient, so every coordinate takes a step of about the learning rate whatever its scale. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**ROC curve**: the curve of the true positive rate against the false positive rate as the decision threshold moves over every value; its area equals the probability that a random positive is scored above a random negative, counting ties as one half. *([Measuring Models: Metrics and Calibration](v02-learning/06-metrics.md))*

**roofline model**: the bound that the attainable rate of a computation on a machine is the smaller of the machine's peak arithmetic rate and its arithmetic intensity times its memory bandwidth, drawn as a slanted line that meets a flat one at the ridge point. *([Memory Bandwidth, Compute and the Roofline](v04-computation/03-roofline.md))*

**RoPE scaling**: changing the rotation rates of the rotary table (and sometimes the magnitude of the rotated vectors) so that a model trained on one length can be run at a longer one, by dividing all rates, a geometric ramp of them or a different rule for each pair. *([Long Context](v06-language-models/08-long-context.md))*

**rotary position embedding**: a scheme that cuts each query and key into pairs of channels and rotates the pair $m$ of position $i$ by the angle $i\,\omega_m$ after the projections, so that every attention score depends on the two positions only through their offset. *([Positional Information](v05-sequences/08-positions.md))*

**rotation matrix**: an orthogonal matrix with determinant $+1$; in the plane $\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}$, and rotations compose by adding their angles. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**rounding error**: the difference between an exact result and the stored number nearest to it; for round to nearest, ties to even, its relative size is at most $u$ for results inside the normal range, and every arithmetic operation commits one. *([Floating Point and Numerical Error](v01-mathematics/15-floating-point.md))*

**router**: the small linear map, followed by a softmax or a sigmoid, that scores every expert for a token so that a selection can be made. *([Mixture of Experts](v06-language-models/04-mixture-of-experts.md))*

**row-major layout**: storing a tensor in memory with the last index changing fastest, so that the element $(i_0, \dots, i_{R-1})$ sits at offset $\sum_k i_k s_k$ with $s_k$ the product of the sizes to its right. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

## S

**safetensors**: a checkpoint format of an unsigned 64-bit little-endian length, that many bytes of JSON mapping each tensor name to its element type, shape and byte offsets, and then the raw bytes of every tensor, back to back. *([Importing Pretrained Models and Proving Parity](v06-language-models/02-importing-models.md))*

**sample mean**: the average of the observations in a sample; it is an unbiased estimator of the true mean, and the accuracy, the mean loss and a minibatch gradient are all sample means. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**sampling from a distribution**: producing values whose long-run frequencies follow a given distribution from uniform random numbers, by a cumulative-sum lookup for a table, inverting the cumulative distribution, a transform such as Box-Muller, or rejection. *([Randomness on a Deterministic Machine](v01-mathematics/17-randomness.md))*

**sampling theorem**: a signal whose frequencies are all below half the sampling rate is completely determined by its samples, and is rebuilt between them as the sum of the samples weighted by a sinc. *([Sound and Sampling](v09-audio/01-sound.md))*

**saved activations**: the values of the forward pass that are kept in memory because the backward pass reads them. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**scalar multiplication**: multiplying every entry of a vector by one number, which stretches, shrinks or flips the arrow. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**scale and zero point**: the pair $(\Delta, q_0)$ of a group: the distance between neighbouring levels and the code that stands for the number 0, chosen so that the codes cover the group's range and 0 is exactly a code. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**scaled dot-product attention**: the layer in which every query is compared with every key by a dot product divided by the square root of their width, a softmax along each row turns the scores into weights, and the weighted sums of the values are the output, $\mathrm{softmax}(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top/\sqrt{d_k})\mathbf{V}$. *([Self-Attention](v05-sequences/07-self-attention.md))*

**scaling laws**: measured relations, close to power laws, between the loss of a language model and its parameters, its training tokens and its compute, with the compute estimate $6Pn_{\mathrm{tok}}$ and the finding of about 20 tokens per parameter for a fixed compute; findings of particular studies under their assumptions. *([Counting Parameters, FLOPs and Memory](v06-language-models/10-model-cost.md))*

**score function**: the slope of the logarithm of a density, $\partial \ln p_t(x)/\partial x$, which points toward higher probability; for noised data it equals minus the conditional mean of the noise divided by $b_t$. *([Diffusion Models](v08-image-generation/05-diffusion.md))*

**seed**: the number from which a generator's starting state is computed; the same seed gives the same stream, and a seed used by a run must be recorded for the run to be repeated. *([Randomness on a Deterministic Machine](v01-mathematics/17-randomness.md))*

**selection cache**: the stored map from a key of device identity, driver version, source digest and shape bucket to the candidate chosen, kept between runs so that a measurement is paid once and discarded when any part of the key changes. *([Choosing the Fastest Correct Kernel](v04-computation/10-kernel-selection.md))*

**semantic segmentation**: assigning a class to every pixel of an image, so that the output is a label map of the picture's own size; a classifier run once per pixel, scored by the intersection over union of the classes' pixel sets. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**sentence embedding**: one vector that represents a whole text, obtained by pooling the per-token vectors of an encoder (the mean over the real tokens, or the row of a designated first token) so that two texts can be compared by the cosine of their vectors. *([Bidirectional Encoders and Embedding Models](v05-sequences/14-encoders.md))*

**sequence packing**: laying the tokens of many documents end to end in one stream and cutting it into rows of a fixed length, with the targets one place later and a padded, masked last row, so that almost every position of every row does useful work. *([Training a GPT from Scratch](v05-sequences/10-training-gpt.md))*

**set**: a collection of distinct elements, written with braces and combined by union, intersection and difference. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**shader translation**: rewriting a kernel from its own language into the form a device accepts so that it still computes what the source computes, which requires keeping every promise the language makes (clamped bounds, wrapping integers, barrier and return semantics, zeroed workgroup memory, layout) that the target does not make by itself. *([One Program, Many Devices](v04-computation/09-backends.md))*

**shape**: the list of the sizes of a tensor's axes, outermost first; the number of elements is their product. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**shared expert**: an expert outside the routing that every token uses, whose output is added to the routed sum, so that what all tokens need is not copied across the routed experts. *([Mixture of Experts](v06-language-models/04-mixture-of-experts.md))*

**shared memory**: the small, fast, on-chip memory of a compute unit that all invocations of one workgroup can read and write and no other workgroup can see, a cache whose contents the programmer chooses. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**shared preprocessing**: the discipline that every preprocessing step (rounding, layout, colour conversion, resampling, padding, normalization) has one implementation used by every model, with the differences between models expressed as parameters in data and checked against the reference, not as copies of code. *([Images as Data](v07-vision/01-images.md))*

**short convolution**: a causal filter of a few taps applied to each channel separately along the sequence, so that every token is mixed with its few predecessors before the recurrence; it needs the last $K - 1$ inputs as a small state when decoding. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**short-time Fourier transform**: the array of Fourier transforms of the frames of a signal, frames of $N$ samples taken every $H$ samples, each weighted by a window, so that time and frequency are both visible. *([Spectrograms and the Mel Scale](v09-audio/02-spectrograms.md))*

**shuffling**: rearranging a list into an order chosen uniformly among all $n!$ orders, correctly done by swapping each position from the end with a uniformly chosen position at or before it (Fisher-Yates). *([Randomness on a Deterministic Machine](v01-mathematics/17-randomness.md))*

**sigmoid**: the function $\sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z})$ that maps any real number to $(0, 1)$ and is the inverse of the logit; its slope is $\sigma(1 - \sigma)$, at most $1/4$. *([Classification and Logistic Regression](v02-learning/03-logistic-regression.md))*

**silu**: the sigmoid linear unit $z\,\sigma(z)$ (also called swish), the input times the logistic sigmoid of the input, smooth, with a slope that overshoots $1$ before settling to it. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**SIMD**: single instruction, multiple data: an instruction that applies the same operation to all the lanes of a wide register at once, for example eight f32 additions in one 256-bit instruction. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**SIMT execution**: single instruction, multiple threads: the hardware issues each instruction once for a fixed group of threads, each applying it to its own registers, so a program is written for one thread and the group's lanes are filled by the hardware. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**singular value decomposition**: the factorisation $\mathbf{A} = \mathbf{U}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{V}^\top$ of any matrix into a rotation, a stretch by non-negative singular values and a second rotation. *([Eigenvalues, Rotations and Low-Rank Structure](v01-mathematics/06-decompositions.md))*

**sinusoid**: a wave $A\cos(2\pi f t + \varphi)$ described by an amplitude $A$ (its largest value), a frequency $f$ (cycles per second) and a phase $\varphi$ (where in its cycle it stands at time zero); a cosine and a sine are the same sinusoid a quarter period apart. *([Complex Numbers, Frequencies and the Fourier Transform](v01-mathematics/14-fourier.md))*

**sinusoidal encoding**: a position vector made of sines and cosines at a geometric scale of rates, $\sin(i\omega_m)$ and $\cos(i\omega_m)$, which needs no training and has, for every offset, a fixed linear map from the vector at one position to the vector at another. *([Positional Information](v05-sequences/08-positions.md))*

**sliding-window attention**: attention in which a query reads only the last $n_{\mathrm{win}}$ keys, itself included, so the cache of the layer is bounded by the window; a stack of such layers reaches $L(n_{\mathrm{win}} - 1) + 1$ positions. *([Attention Variants: Sharing and Compressing Keys](v06-language-models/03-attention-variants.md))*

**softmax**: the function that turns a vector of real scores into a probability vector by exponentiating each score and dividing by the sum of the exponentials, so that the outputs are positive, add to one and keep the order of the scores. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**softmax-cross-entropy**: the loss of a classifier computed directly from its scores and the true class as the log-sum-exp of the scores minus the score of the true class; it is the negative log-likelihood of the true class under the softmax, and its gradient with respect to the scores is the probability vector minus the one-hot target. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**sorting**: rearranging a list into non-decreasing order; comparison sorts need $\Omega(n \log n)$ comparisons in the worst case and merge sort achieves it, while sorts that use the values of integer keys as addresses can be linear. *([Algorithms, Cost and Complexity](v01-mathematics/16-algorithms.md))*

**sparse attention pattern**: the rule that gives each query the set of keys it reads, instead of all earlier keys, so that attention is a softmax over those keys only; fixed patterns depend on positions alone, such as a window, global tokens, a stride or blocks. *([Sparse Attention](v06-language-models/06-sparse-attention.md))*

**spatiotemporal attention**: self-attention in which the tokens of a clip, placed on a grid of frame, row and column, attend to one another across all three axes. *([Generating Video](v10-video-and-3d/02-video-generation.md))*

**speaker embedding**: a vector of fixed length computed from a recording of any length, such that recordings of one voice are close in cosine and recordings of different voices are not. *([Who Is Speaking](v09-audio/05-speaker-embeddings.md))*

**special tokens**: ids that stand for no piece of text, such as the beginning or end of a sequence, padding, an unknown piece or the markers of a chat turn, matched from their literals before ordinary encoding and never to be produced from text a client wrote. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**speech encoder**: the stack that turns the frames of a log-mel spectrogram into fewer rows of one width, each informed by its neighbours, ready for an alignment loss or a decoder. *([Speech Recognition](v09-audio/04-speech-recognition.md))*

**speech tokenizer**: a network trained, with a supervised target such as the transcript and not by reconstruction, to turn speech into discrete tokens that carry what is said and little of who says it or how. *([Speech Synthesis](v09-audio/06-speech-synthesis.md))*

**stable-softmax**: the softmax computed after subtracting the largest score from every score, which gives the same probabilities but keeps every exponent at most zero, so nothing overflows and the sum is at least one. *([Softmax, Logits and Cross-Entropy](v03-neural-networks/03-softmax.md))*

**standard error**: the standard deviation of an estimator over repeated samples, the typical size of its error; for the sample mean it is $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$, estimated by $s/\sqrt{n}$. *([Statistics: Learning Facts from Samples](v01-mathematics/12-statistics.md))*

**state-space model**: a layer whose state evolves under a linear system in continuous time, $\mathbf{h}' = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{h} + \mathbf{B}x$, discretized into a recurrence $\mathbf{h}_t = \bar{\mathbf{A}}\mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \bar{\mathbf{B}}x_t$ with a step size that may depend on the input. *([Linear Attention, Recurrence and Hybrid Models](v06-language-models/05-linear-attention.md))*

**stochastic gradient descent**: gradient descent that steps along the gradient of a small random batch of examples instead of the whole training set, $\theta \leftarrow \theta - \eta\,\mathbf{g}_t$, an unbiased but noisy estimate of the full step. *([Optimizers: From SGD to AdamW](v03-neural-networks/07-optimizers.md))*

**storage buffer**: a large array in device memory that a kernel reads or reads and writes, whose element type the kernel declares and whose length the host chooses when it binds the buffer. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**straight-through estimator**: the rule that passes the gradient at a quantizer's output to its input unchanged, written $\mathbf{z} + \mathrm{sg}[\mathbf{z}_q - \mathbf{z}]$ with a stop-gradient $\mathrm{sg}$; it replaces a derivative that is zero by a biased one that trains the encoder. *([Discrete Latents and Vector Quantization](v08-image-generation/03-vector-quantization.md))*

**streaming speech output**: speech that begins to leave the model while the text it says is still being written and its own later frames are still being drawn, so that the work before the first sound is that of a prefix of the reply and not of the whole reply. *([Models That Listen, See and Speak](v09-audio/08-omni-models.md))*

**stride**: the distance in memory, counted in elements, between two neighbours along one axis; a view is described by one stride per axis, and stride 0 repeats one number. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**subgroup**: the group of consecutive invocations of a workgroup, 32 in this book's model, that the hardware executes with one instruction at a time. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

**summation notation**: the symbol $\sum_{i=a}^{b} x_i$ for the sum of the terms $x_i$ as the index $i$ runs from $a$ to $b$. *([Numbers, Quantities and Notation](v01-mathematics/01-numbers.md))*

**super-resolution**: producing a picture with more pixels than the one in hand, by estimating the detail that the downsampling removed; because many pictures share one downsampling, the output is a choice among them. *([Restoration and Super-Resolution](v08-image-generation/12-restoration.md))*

**supervised learning**: learning from examples that all carry labels, in order to predict the label of a new example. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**SwiGLU**: the gated feed-forward network $(\mathrm{silu}(\mathbf{x}\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{gate}}) \odot \mathbf{x}\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{up}})\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{down}}$, whose hidden width of $8D/3$ gives it as many parameters as a plain network of width $4D$. *([The Transformer Block](v05-sequences/09-transformer-block.md))*

**Swin transformer**: a hierarchical vision transformer whose attention is confined to non-overlapping windows and whose windows are displaced by half a window in alternate layers, so that information crosses window borders at the same cost per layer. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**symmetry-breaking**: starting the units of a layer with different weights, by random draws, so that their gradients differ; units that start identical stay identical forever. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

## T

**tanh-activation**: the hyperbolic tangent used as a neuron's activation, a smooth step from $-1$ to $1$ equal to $2\sigma(2z) - 1$ with slope $1 - \tanh^2(z)$, centred on zero and saturating for large $|z|$. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**Taylor expansion**: the polynomial that matches a function's value and first derivatives at a point, such as $f(a) + f'(a)h + \tfrac{1}{2}f''(a)h^2$, whose error is of the order of the first term dropped. *([Gradients, Jacobians and Many Variables](v01-mathematics/08-multivariable-calculus.md))*
