**teacher forcing**: training a sequence model at every position with the true earlier tokens as its context, instead of its own earlier predictions, so that a sequence of $T$ tokens gives $T$ independent training examples in one pass. *([Language Modeling](v05-sequences/04-language-modeling.md))*

**temperature**: a positive number $\tau$ by which the logits are divided before the softmax; low values sharpen the distribution toward the largest token, high values flatten it toward uniform, and the entropy rises with it. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**tensor**: an array of numbers with any number of axes (zero for a scalar, one for a vector, two for a matrix), described by its shape. *([Arrays, Shapes, Strides and Broadcasting](v01-mathematics/05-arrays.md))*

**tensor core**: a hardware unit that multiplies two small fixed-size matrices and adds a third in one operation, usually with narrow inputs and a wider accumulator, raising the peak arithmetic rate of a device for matrix products. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**test set**: rows used once, after every choice is made, to report the final score of the chosen model; looking at it more than once turns it into a validation set. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**test-dimension choice**: choosing the sizes of the model a test runs on (batch, features, widths, heads) all different and above 1, so that bugs that confuse two sizes or depend on a size of 1 change the result. *([Proving Gradients Correct](v03-neural-networks/06-gradient-checking.md))*

**text-encoder conditioning**: turning a prompt into the generator's input with a separate pretrained text encoder that is run forward at generation time, so that the denoiser sees the prompt only through the arrays the encoder produced; the tokenizer, the window, the layer read and the padding are then part of the denoiser's input contract. *([Conditioning on Text](v08-image-generation/09-text-conditioning.md))*

**text-to-speech**: the task of turning a text, and usually a description of a voice, into the waveform of someone saying it. *([Speech Synthesis](v09-audio/06-speech-synthesis.md))*

**thinker-talker split**: the division of an omni model's decoding into a Thinker, which reads the whole request and writes the reply as text, and a Talker, which reads the reply's words and the Thinker's states at the media rows and writes the speech as codec frames, with its own weights, vocabulary and clock. *([Models That Listen, See and Speak](v09-audio/08-omni-models.md))*

**thread parallelism**: using several threads, each running on its own core with its own registers and first caches and sharing the later caches and memory, to carry out the pieces of one computation at the same time. *([The CPU: Cores, Caches and Vectors](v04-computation/02-cpu.md))*

**tied embeddings**: using one table both to embed the input tokens and as the output layer that scores the tokens, so that the logits are $\mathbf{H}\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{emb}}^\top$, which saves one table of $V D$ parameters and gives that table the gradient of both uses. *([Embeddings](v05-sequences/03-embeddings.md))*

**tiled attention**: the schedule that computes attention for a block of query rows by walking tiles of keys and values through fast memory, forming the block of scores of each tile only on chip and folding it into the running state of its rows, so that no score matrix is ever written to global memory. *([Attention Without the Quadratic Memory](v05-sequences/13-flash-attention.md))*

**tiled matmul**: the matrix product computed one tile of the output at a time, with the matching tiles of the two inputs staged in a fast memory so that each number loaded is used once per row or column of the tile, cutting the loads from $2n^3$ to $2n^3/T$ for a tile of side $T$. *([Making Matrix Multiplication Fast](v04-computation/06-matmul.md))*

**time-delay network**: a network of one-dimensional convolutions along time, whose weights are shared across time and whose units read a layer at several delayed moments, so that a deeper unit sees a longer stretch of the signal. *([Who Is Speaking](v09-audio/05-speaker-embeddings.md))*

**timestep embedding**: the vector made from the scalar noise level by a sinusoidal encoding (cosines of the scaled level at a ladder of rates, then the sines) and a small network, so that a model built from vectors can read how noisy its input is. *([Denoiser Architectures: U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers](v08-image-generation/08-denoiser-architectures.md))*

**timestep shift**: the map $\sigma' = k\sigma/(1 + (k - 1)\sigma)$, or with $k = e^\mu$ the exponential form $e^\mu/(e^\mu + 1/\sigma - 1)$, that moves the sampling steps toward noise while keeping $0$ and $1$ fixed, so that larger images, which carry more redundant pixels per noise level, spend their steps where the commitment happens. *([Flow Matching and Rectified Flow](v08-image-generation/06-flow-matching.md))*

**token**: the unit a model counts, one piece of the text a tokenizer cuts, with an integer id in the vocabulary; a token can be a character, a word, a part of a word or a single byte. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**top-k gating**: choosing the $k$ experts with the largest router scores for a token and combining their outputs with weights that come from those scores, normalized to sum to 1. *([Mixture of Experts](v06-language-models/04-mixture-of-experts.md))*

**top-k sampling**: keeping only the $k$ most probable tokens, setting the rest to zero and renormalizing before the draw. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**top-p sampling**: keeping the smallest set of most probable tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a threshold, also called nucleus sampling, so that the number of tokens kept follows how spread out the distribution is. *([Decoding: Turning Probabilities into Text](v05-sequences/11-decoding.md))*

**train-vs-eval-mode**: the two behaviours of a layer that has a state of its own: in train mode batch normalization uses the batch statistics and updates its running averages, in eval mode it uses the running averages and changes nothing. *([Normalization Layers](v03-neural-networks/10-normalization.md))*

**training memory formula**: the sum for a training step: for each parameter its value, gradient, optimizer slots and master copy (16 bytes under Adam in either f32 or mixed precision), plus the numbers kept per token for the backward pass, reduced by recomputation, plus scratch. *([Counting Parameters, FLOPs and Memory](v06-language-models/10-model-cost.md))*

**training set**: the rows used to fit a model's parameters, and no other decisions; the error on it is a flattering estimate of the error on new rows. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**training throughput**: the rate at which a training run consumes tokens, stated as the FLOPs and bytes each token costs and the fraction of the device's roofline that the run reaches, not as seconds. *([Training a GPT from Scratch](v05-sequences/10-training-gpt.md))*

**transducer**: a recogniser with an encoder, a predictor over the labels written so far and a joint network over every node of the lattice of rows and labels, in which a blank moves to the next row and a label is written on the same row. *([Speech Recognition](v09-audio/04-speech-recognition.md))*

**transformer block**: the repeating unit of a transformer, one attention sublayer and one feed-forward sublayer, each with its normalization and its addition to the residual stream. *([The Transformer Block](v05-sequences/09-transformer-block.md))*

**transpose**: the matrix $\mathbf{A}^\top$ with rows and columns swapped; $(\mathbf{A}\mathbf{B})^\top = \mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{A}^\top$. *([Matrices as Linear Maps](v01-mathematics/04-matrices.md))*

**transposed convolution**: the adjoint of a strided convolution, used as a layer that enlarges a map: every input value stamps the kernel onto the output at stride spacing and overlapping stamps add, so unequal overlap (unequal phase sums of the kernel) gives a checkerboard pattern. *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**tree reduction**: a parallel reduction that combines the values in pairs, then the pairs in pairs, so that $n$ values need $n - 1$ combinations in only $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ dependent steps; inside a workgroup it is a loop over strides with a barrier after each step. *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

**triangulation**: finding a 3D point from its images in two or more cameras of known pose, as the point where the rays meet or, with noise, the one that fits them best, whose depth error falls as the angle between the rays grows. *([Structure from Motion and Multi-View Stereo](v10-video-and-3d/04-structure-from-motion.md))*

**two's complement**: the representation of negative whole numbers in which the pattern of $-x$ is $2^n - x$ (the bits of $x$ inverted, plus one), so that the same addition works for both signs, the top bit is the sign, and the range is $-2^{n-1} \dots 2^{n-1} - 1$. *([Bits and Number Formats](v04-computation/01-number-formats.md))*

**two-dimensional convolution**: the operation that gives each output value as the sum of the products of a small kernel's weights with the image values under it, the same kernel at every position and, in deep learning, without turning the kernel over (a cross-correlation). *([Convolution](v07-vision/02-convolution.md))*

**two-pass reduction**: the reduction of an array longer than a workgroup by two dispatches, one in which every workgroup writes a partial result for its slice and a second that reduces the partials, the end of the first dispatch serving as the barrier between workgroups that a dispatch cannot have. *([Parallel Reductions, Scans and Sorting](v04-computation/07-reductions.md))*

## U

**U-Net**: an encoder-decoder network that halves the resolution of a map level by level, then doubles it back, joining each level of the way up to the map of the same size from the way down by a skip connection, so that its output has the size of its input; the denoiser of SDXL has three levels and a stack of nine skips. *([Denoiser Architectures: U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers](v08-image-generation/08-denoiser-architectures.md))*

**underfitting**: a model too restricted to represent the pattern, so that its error is high on the training rows and on new rows alike. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**Unicode**: the standard that numbers every character of every writing system once (its code point, from U+0000 to U+10FFFF) and records its properties, such as category, combining class and case; what a reader sees as one character is a grapheme cluster, a run of one or more code points (a letter with its accent, a flag, a family emoji) grouped by rules of the standard. *([Text as Data](v05-sequences/01-text.md))*

**uniform parameters**: the small block of constants, the same for every invocation and read-only, that the host writes into a separate buffer for a kernel: element counts, scalars, shapes and strides. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**unigram tokenizer**: a tokenizer whose vocabulary carries a probability for each piece and which cuts a word into the segmentation of highest total log-probability, found by dynamic programming; it is trained by re-estimating the probabilities and pruning pieces. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**universal-approximation**: the theorem that, for any continuous function on a closed bounded set and any tolerance, some one-hidden-layer network with a non-polynomial activation stays within that tolerance everywhere on the set; it guarantees that the weights exist, not how many units they need or how to find them. *([Multilayer Networks](v03-neural-networks/02-mlp.md))*

**unsupervised learning**: learning from examples without labels, to find structure such as groups in the features themselves. *([The Learning Problem](v02-learning/01-learning-problem.md))*

**untied output head**: an output matrix $\mathbf{W}_{\mathrm{out}}$ of shape $[V, D]$ that is separate from the embedding table, so each has its own parameters and its own gradient. *([Anatomy of a Modern Decoder](v06-language-models/01-modern-decoder.md))*

**upsampling**: any operation that takes a map to one with more positions: repetition, interpolation, a transposed convolution, a pixel shuffle or a learned combination of neighbours, each with its own cost and its own artifacts. *([Dense Prediction: Segmentation and Depth](v07-vision/05-dense-prediction.md))*

**UTF-8**: the encoding that writes each Unicode scalar value as 1 to 4 bytes whose leading bits announce the sequence's length, compatible with ASCII, self-synchronizing and ordered like the code points; its decoder is a state machine of eight states. *([Text as Data](v05-sequences/01-text.md))*

## V

**v-prediction**: asking the network for the velocity $v = a_t\varepsilon - b_t x_0$, a rotation of the clean value and the noise that keeps the error of the implied clean value bounded at every noise level. *([Diffusion Models](v08-image-generation/05-diffusion.md))*

**validation set**: rows kept apart from fitting and used to choose between models (degree, penalty, learning rate, when to stop); the score of the chosen model on it is optimistic, because it was chosen for its score. *([Generalization, Overfitting and Honest Evaluation](v02-learning/05-generalization.md))*

**vanishing-gradient**: the gradient reaching the early layers of a deep network is a tiny fraction of the one at the top, because it is a product of layer Jacobians whose factors are below one; those layers do not learn. *([Training Dynamics and Debugging](v03-neural-networks/12-training-dynamics.md))*

**variance**: the expected squared deviation from the mean, $\mathbb{E}[X^2] - \mathbb{E}[X]^2$, which scales by $a^2$ under multiplication by $a$ and adds over independent variables; its square root is the standard deviation. *([Probability: Reasoning Under Uncertainty](v01-mathematics/10-probability.md))*

**variance-preservation**: choosing the scale of the weights so that the typical size of activations (and of gradients) is the same in every layer, neither shrinking nor growing with depth. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

**variational autoencoder**: an autoencoder trained as a latent-variable model by maximizing the evidence lower bound: an encoder that returns the mean and log-variance of a Gaussian over the latent, a draw from it by the reparameterization trick, a decoder that returns a reading, and a loss of reconstruction error plus the KL divergence of the encoder's distribution from the prior. *([Variational Autoencoders](v08-image-generation/02-vae.md))*

**vector**: an ordered list of real numbers, read as data (the features of one example) or as an arrow with a length and a direction. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**vector addition**: adding two vectors of the same length entry by entry; as arrows it is the parallelogram rule. *([Vectors: Lists of Numbers with Geometry](v01-mathematics/03-vectors.md))*

**vector quantization**: replacing a vector by the nearest row of a codebook (smallest squared distance, lowest index on a tie), so that it is stored as one index of $\log_2 K$ bits. *([Discrete Latents and Vector Quantization](v08-image-generation/03-vector-quantization.md))*

**vector-Jacobian product**: the product of a row vector with a Jacobian, computed by a per-operation rule without ever building the Jacobian as a matrix. *([Backpropagation Derived from Scratch](v03-neural-networks/04-backpropagation.md))*

**velocity field**: the average velocity $u(x, \sigma) = \mathbb{E}[\varepsilon - x_0 \mid x_\sigma = x]$ of all the straight lines through a point; following it as an ordinary differential equation carries the standard normal onto the data. *([Flow Matching and Rectified Flow](v08-image-generation/06-flow-matching.md))*

**video autoencoder**: an encoder that turns a clip into a short grid of numbers, smaller in space and in time, and a decoder that turns the grid back into frames. *([Video as Data](v10-video-and-3d/01-video.md))*

**video codec**: a method that stores a clip in few bytes by predicting each frame from earlier ones, coding the prediction error coarsely, and decoding by repeating the same prediction. *([Video as Data](v10-video-and-3d/01-video.md))*

**video diffusion**: diffusion or flow-matching generation on the latent grid of a video: a transformer predicts the velocity of every token of a noised clip, with a position on each of three axes and a timestep for each token, and a sampler turns the noise into a clip's latent. *([Generating Video](v10-video-and-3d/02-video-generation.md))*

**vision projector**: the small trained map, a linear layer or a pair of them around a GELU, sometimes folding a block of neighbouring patches into one row, that takes the rows of a vision tower to the width of a language model's embedding rows so that they can be read like the rows of words. *([Vision-Language Models](v07-vision/09-vlms.md))*

**vision token compression**: reducing the number of tokens that stand for a picture before the stages whose cost grows with that number, the quadratic attention of a global tower and the decoder's prefill and cache; here by a fixed convolution that folds 16 positions into 1, and by the choice of how many views a page gets. *([Reading Documents](v07-vision/10-ocr.md))*

**vision transformer**: a model that applies a stack of unmasked transformer blocks to a sequence of patch embeddings with position information added, and reads out a class token or the mean of the tokens. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**vocabulary**: the list of every piece a tokenizer can produce, each with its id; its size $V$ is the number of rows the model's embedding table needs. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**vocoder**: a network that turns a spectrogram back into a waveform, supplying the phase and the fine periodic structure that the spectrogram discards. *([Speech Synthesis](v09-audio/06-speech-synthesis.md))*

**voice cloning**: making a synthesiser speak in the voice of a person from whom it has only a short recording, without training on that person. *([Speech Synthesis](v09-audio/06-speech-synthesis.md))*

## W

**warmup runs**: the leading runs of a repeated measurement whose cost is dominated by a start-up transient (building pipelines, first-touch memory, cold caches, a clock that has not ramped up) and is not the cost of the steady state; they are detected and kept out of the summary, or reported as a separate cold row. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**waveform**: the pressure of a sound, or the voltage of a microphone that follows it, written as a function of time. *([Sound and Sampling](v09-audio/01-sound.md))*

**weight decay**: shrinking every weight toward zero by the fraction $\eta\lambda$ at each step, as a regularizer of a neural network; the L2 penalty of Volume II, applied directly to the weights in the decoupled form of chapter 7. *([Regularization in Neural Networks](v03-neural-networks/11-regularization.md))*

**weight streaming**: moving the weights of a stage, or of a window of blocks, onto a device when their turn comes and off when it ends, so that the device holds the largest part and not the sum of all of them, at the price of the bytes uploaded each time. *([Latent Diffusion Systems End to End](v08-image-generation/10-latent-diffusion-systems.md))*

**weight-name mapping**: the table and rules that turn the tensor names, orientations and groupings of a published layout into those of an implementation: renames, cuts of fused matrices and transposes, checked before they run for coverage and shape. *([Importing Pretrained Models and Proving Parity](v06-language-models/02-importing-models.md))*

**weight-only quantization**: storing the weights as low-bit codes with scales while the activations stay in a higher-precision format, decoding the codes inside the matrix product so that the bytes read, and not the arithmetic, shrink. *([Quantization: Fewer Bits per Weight](v04-computation/12-quantization.md))*

**weight-shared depth**: using the same parameters at more than one depth of a network, so that its depth, and the arithmetic per token, can grow without the parameters growing; every use needs its own activations and its own cache. *([Looped and Recurrent-Depth Transformers](v06-language-models/07-recurrent-depth.md))*

**WGSL**: the WebGPU Shading Language, a small kernel language that compiles to the native graphics interfaces and in which the book writes its kernel examples. *([Writing Compute Kernels](v04-computation/05-compute-kernels.md))*

**whole-pass measurement**: the time of the whole unit of work a user waits for, with every dispatch, wait, copy and host-side step the real use performs inside the bracket, repeated and summarized with its spread; the number by which a change is judged. *([Measuring Performance Honestly](v04-computation/11-profiling.md))*

**window function**: a list of weights applied to the samples of a frame before it is transformed, falling to zero at the ends so that the frame's edges do not leak energy into every frequency. *([Spectrograms and the Mel Scale](v09-audio/02-spectrograms.md))*

**windowed attention**: attention in which each token reads only the tokens in its own non-overlapping window of the grid, so that the cost grows linearly with the number of tokens; shifting the windows between layers, or adding a few global layers, lets information cross the window borders. *([Vision Transformers](v07-vision/06-vision-transformers.md))*

**WordPiece**: a tokenizer that cuts a word by greedy longest match from the left, marks every piece after the first with `##`, and turns a word it cannot cover into `[UNK]`; its vocabulary is chosen to raise the likelihood of the training text. *([Tokenization](v05-sequences/02-tokenization.md))*

**workgroup**: a set of invocations of one dispatch that run together on one compute unit, share an on-chip memory and can wait for each other at a barrier, while different workgroups are independent. *([The GPU: Thousands of Small Workers](v04-computation/04-gpu.md))*

## X

**xavier-initialization**: drawing the weights of a layer with variance $2/(n_{\mathrm{in}} + n_{\mathrm{out}})$, the harmonic mean of the forward-preserving and backward-preserving variances, for units that behave like the identity near zero. *([Initialization: Where Training Starts](v03-neural-networks/09-initialization.md))*

**XOR problem**: the fact that the exclusive-or of two bits, whose two classes sit on opposite diagonals of a square, is not linearly separable and so no single threshold neuron computes it. *([The Neuron and the Perceptron](v03-neural-networks/01-perceptron.md))*

## Y

**YaRN**: a rope scaling that gives each frequency pair a rate between its original and its original divided by the extension factor, by the number of turns it makes over the trained length, and multiplies the cosine and sine of every pair by $0.1\ln s + 1$ to restore the sharpness of the softmax. *([Long Context](v06-language-models/08-long-context.md))*

## Z

**zero convolution**: a $1 \times 1$ convolution whose weights and bias start at exactly zero, so that a branch ending in it adds nothing at the first step, yet its own weights already have a gradient, and the layers behind it receive one from the second step on. *([Control, Identity and Adapters](v08-image-generation/11-control-and-identity.md))*

**zero-shot classification**: assigning an input to the class whose caption vector is nearest, with the class vectors computed at the time of the question from sentences naming the classes (averaged over several templates), so that classes need no labelled examples and no trained weight of their own. *([Contrastive Vision-Language Learning](v07-vision/08-clip.md))*
